★ what_this_is: CAPTURED DATA -- the live schema of this database, read from the DB itself. Not a rulebook: it records what the schema IS, never what it should be. Rules governing it: iba/config/utility/DBSchema_maintenance.json (util.dbschema). Every description is derived from the `profile` beside it (dbschema.description-from-data).

book_code_variants.description: Alias table mapping the many book abbreviation forms encountered in source data onto a single books row, so that '1Chr', '1Ki' and '1Kgs' all resolve to the same book. 112 aliases cover all 66 books, with the busiest books carrying up to three variants each.
book_code_variants.sql:
CREATE TABLE book_code_variants (
        code    TEXT    PRIMARY KEY,
        book_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES books(id)
    )

columns.name: code
columns.description: The alias string as it appears in incoming data, e.g. '1Ch', '1Chr', '1Cor', '1Kgs'. It is the primary key, so one spelling can never map to two books.

columns.name: book_id
columns.description: The books row the alias resolves to. Every one of the 66 books is represented; some carry three aliases and most carry one or two.

books.description: The 66 books of the Bible as canonical reference data: name, testament, canonical order and several code forms used to parse and render verse references. Fully populated and stable — every row was written in a single load on 2026-03-16 and none has been touched since.
books.sql:
CREATE TABLE books (
    id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name        TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,           -- e.g. "John"
    abbreviation TEXT   NOT NULL UNIQUE,           -- e.g. "Jn"
    testament   TEXT    NOT NULL                   -- "OT" or "NT"
                CHECK (testament IN ('OT', 'NT')),
    book_order  INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE            -- canonical order 1–66
, full_name TEXT, short_code TEXT, verse_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, last_updated TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now')))

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the book, 1-66, and the target of book_code_variants.book_id. Runs in canonical order, so it matches book_order across all 66 rows.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The book's common name as used throughout the programme, e.g. '1 Chronicles', '1 John'. Unique across all 66 rows and the usual human-readable label.

columns.name: abbreviation
columns.description: Three-character book abbreviation, e.g. '1Ch', '1Co', '1Jn'. Unique per book; note it differs from short_code for some books (1Co here versus 1Cor there).

columns.name: testament
columns.description: Which testament the book belongs to. Constrained by CHECK to OT or NT; 39 OT and 27 NT.

columns.name: book_order
columns.description: Canonical position of the book, 1-66. Unique, and identical to id in every row, so it is effectively redundant with the primary key.

columns.name: full_name
columns.description: The formal descriptive title, e.g. 'The Acts of the Apostles', 'The Book of Amos'. Populated for all 66 books; presentational rather than a lookup key.

profile.max: The Third Epistle General of John

columns.name: short_code
columns.description: The book code used for reference matching, e.g. '1Ch', '1Cor', '1Jn'. Unique, and the canonical form that book_code_variants aliases resolve towards.

columns.name: verse_count
columns.description: Total verses in the book. Populated for 64 books but left at the default 0 for Obadiah and Philemon, so it cannot be relied on as a complete verse census.

columns.name: last_updated
columns.description: When the book row was last written. Every one of the 66 rows carries the identical value 2026-03-16T12:44:41, confirming a single bulk load and no subsequent edit.

characteristic.description: The named characteristics belonging to each cluster — the distinct inner-being traits a cluster resolves into, each with a definition. 277 rows across 35 clusters, layered from several eras: 53 backfilled 1:1 from sub-groups in May, and 78 added in July as explicitly PROVISIONAL top-down exemplars. Note that cluster_code has indexes but no foreign key to cluster.
characteristic.sql:
CREATE TABLE characteristic (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                cluster_code TEXT NOT NULL,
                char_seq INTEGER NOT NULL,
                short_name TEXT NOT NULL,
                definition TEXT NOT NULL,
                source TEXT,
                version TEXT DEFAULT 'v1',
                notes TEXT,
                delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                last_updated_date TEXT NOT NULL,
                UNIQUE(cluster_code, char_seq),
                UNIQUE(cluster_code, short_name)
            )

columns.name: short_name
columns.description: The characteristic's name, unique within its cluster. Mostly a single concept ('Wonder'), but some rows carry a letter prefix ('A - Felt shame at falsified trust'), showing two naming conventions in one column.

characteristic_subgroup.description: The many-to-many join between a characteristic and the cluster sub-groups that carry it, recording why the pairing holds. In practice it is near 1:1 — 145 distinct sub-groups over 146 rows — and its qualifier notes confirm most rows are single-sub-group representations rather than genuine fan-out.
characteristic_subgroup.sql:
CREATE TABLE characteristic_subgroup (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                characteristic_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
                cluster_subgroup_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
                qualifier_note TEXT,
                is_partial INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
                partial_register_note TEXT,
                delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                last_updated_date TEXT NOT NULL,
                UNIQUE(characteristic_id, cluster_subgroup_id),
                FOREIGN KEY (characteristic_id) REFERENCES characteristic(id),
                FOREIGN KEY (cluster_subgroup_id) REFERENCES cluster_subgroup(id)
            )

columns.description: Why this characteristic is served by this sub-group. Frequently the boilerplate 'Single-sub-group representation (sub-group = characteristic 1:1).', which itself documents that the join is mostly degenerate.

cluster.description: The 49 top-level thematic groupings of the study (47 M-codes plus FLAG and T2), each naming a domain of the inner life such as Anger, Wisdom or Peace. Keyed on the M-code itself rather than a surrogate id, so the code is the stable identifier used across the cluster tables.
cluster.sql:
CREATE TABLE cluster (
                    cluster_code      TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                    description       TEXT,
                    gloss             TEXT NOT NULL,
                    source            TEXT,
                    bucket            TEXT,
                    status            TEXT,
                    version           TEXT,
                    last_updated_date TEXT

columns.name: description

cluster_finding.description: The catalogue-prompted findings layer: one row per observation question asked of a cluster (or of a characteristic, sub-group or verse-context group within it), holding the answer text. At ~20k rows across only 15 clusters it is the bulk output of the pre-reset method, and 1,633 rows are delete-flagged following the 2026-06-11 catalogue restructure.
cluster_finding.sql:
CREATE TABLE "cluster_finding" (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                obs_id INTEGER NOT NULL
                    REFERENCES wa_obs_question_catalogue(obs_id),
                cluster_code TEXT NOT NULL
                    REFERENCES cluster(cluster_code),
                characteristic_id INTEGER
                    REFERENCES characteristic(id),
                cluster_subgroup_id INTEGER
                    REFERENCES cluster_subgroup(id),
                vcg_scope TEXT,
                finding_status TEXT NOT NULL
                    CHECK (finding_status IN ('finding','silent','gap','cluster_synthesis')),
                finding_text TEXT,
                source_file TEXT,
                version TEXT,
                notes TEXT,
                delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
                created_at TEXT,
                last_updated_date TEXT, finding_type TEXT, needs_research INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
                UNIQUE (obs_id, cluster_code, characteristic_id, cluster_subgroup_id, vcg_scope, version)
            )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key; the maximum value (20,572) exceeds the row count, so ids have been consumed and rows hard-deleted at some point.

columns.name: obs_id
columns.description: The observation question this finding answers, pointing into the 189-question catalogue; all 189 questions are in use and each is asked ~125-130 times.

columns.name: cluster_code
columns.description: The cluster the finding belongs to. Only 15 clusters have findings, and M10 alone holds 6,426 of ~20k rows.

columns.name: characteristic_id
columns.description: The characteristic the finding is scoped to, where the question was asked at characteristic level; NULL on 2,335 rows asked at cluster level only.

columns.name: cluster_subgroup_id
columns.description: The sub-group the finding is scoped to; NULL on 12,715 of 19,997 rows, so most findings sit above sub-group level.

columns.name: vcg_scope
columns.description: The verse-context group the finding is narrowed to, recorded as a text code such as 'M02-B-VCG-03' rather than an id. Populated on only 477 rows — the finest scope, rarely used.

columns.name: finding_status
columns.description: What the question yielded: 'finding' (16,284) where evidence answered it, 'silent' (1,806) where the corpus said nothing, 'gap' (123) where evidence is missing, or 'cluster_synthesis' (1,784) for synthesis-level answers. The one CHECK-constrained vocabulary in the table.

columns.name: finding_text
columns.description: The finding itself — the prose answer to the question, from a sentence to a long paragraph. 16,862 distinct texts across 19,997 rows, so some answers repeat verbatim.

cluster_observation.description: Write-on-discovery notes made while working a cluster — design rationales, verdicts, synthesis notes and carry-forwards — each addressed to a later phase that should consume it. Unlike cluster_finding these are not prompted by a question; 229 of 276 rows come from the M10 work alone.
cluster_observation.sql:
CREATE TABLE cluster_observation (
                id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                cluster_code TEXT NOT NULL,
                characteristic_id INTEGER,
                cluster_subgroup_id INTEGER,
                source_phase TEXT NOT NULL,
                observation_type TEXT NOT NULL,
                target_phase TEXT,
                title TEXT NOT NULL,
                description TEXT NOT NULL,
                status TEXT DEFAULT 'open',
                resolution_note TEXT,
                raised_date TEXT NOT NULL,
                resolved_date TEXT,
                source_file TEXT,
                delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
                created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
                last_updated_date TEXT NOT NULL,
                FOREIGN KEY (characteristic_id) REFERENCES characteristic(id),
                FOREIGN KEY (cluster_subgroup_id) REFERENCES cluster_subgroup(id)
            )

cluster_subgroup.description: Sub-divisions of a cluster (for example M01-A, M01-BOUNDARY), each carrying a label and a core description that scopes which sense of the cluster theme it covers. engine_run_log.description: One row per engine or patch execution (875 rows, March to July), recording mode, timing, outcome and roll-up counts of what was written. It is the parent audit record that word_run_state, engine_stream_checkpoint and term_fetch_log hang off, and it logs patch applications as well as engine runs.
engine_run_log.sql:
CREATE TABLE engine_run_log (
            id                   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            run_id               TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
            mode                 TEXT    NOT NULL,
            target_registry_ids  TEXT,
            started_at           TEXT    NOT NULL,
            completed_at         TEXT,
            outcome              TEXT,
            words_attempted      INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            words_complete       INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            words_stopped        INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            total_terms_new      INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            total_terms_xref     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            total_verses_inserted INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            total_verses_filtered INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            total_meanings_parsed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            error_detail         TEXT,
            resume_from          TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key. Note it runs to 887 across 875 rows, so a dozen ids have been deleted or never committed.

columns.name: run_id
columns.description: The run's public identifier and the FK target for the child tables. Formats are mixed: most are 'RUN-{timestamp}-{MODE}' or 'PATCH-20260324-004-SESSIONB-V1', but some are plain document slugs such as 'wa-tier-catalogue-refit-update-v1-20260619', so the identifier is not from one scheme.

columns.name: mode
columns.description: What kind of run it was: AUDIT_WORD 522, SESSION_PATCH 311, NEW_WORD 27, GAP_FILL 9, plus 6 rows in lower-case ad-hoc modes ('verse_read_meaning', 'cc_verse_read'). Uncontrolled, and the case inconsistency marks the later hand-run work.

columns.name: target_registry_ids
columns.description: Which registry words the run targeted. Unreliable as a key: 201 rows hold an empty string and 10 hold the literal string 'None', so absence is encoded three different ways.

columns.name: started_at
columns.description: When the run began, ISO-8601 without a zone marker, spanning 2026-03-18 to 2026-07-13. The reliable ordering field for the log.

columns.name: completed_at
columns.description: When the run finished. NULL in 13 rows, which are runs that never recorded completion — consistent with the 12 rows still showing outcome RUNNING.

columns.name: outcome
columns.description: How the run ended: COMPLETE 681, STOPPED 169, RUNNING 12, PARTIAL 7, PASS 5. Uncontrolled, and the set is muddled — PASS duplicates COMPLETE's meaning, and the 12 RUNNING rows are stale rather than live.

columns.name: words_attempted
columns.description: How many registry words the run tried to process. Almost always 1 (539) or 0 (334); two bulk runs attempted 167.

columns.name: words_complete
columns.description: How many words the run finished. 0 in 515 rows and 1 in 359 — so a majority of logged runs completed no word at all, which fits the SESSION_PATCH rows that process no word.

columns.name: words_stopped
columns.description: How many words the run stopped on. Mostly 0 (704) or 1 (169), with two outlier bulk runs recording 293 and 575 stopped words.

columns.name: total_terms_new
columns.description: How many new terms the run inserted. 0 in 577 rows; the rest range up to the dozens, so term creation is concentrated in a minority of runs.

columns.name: total_terms_xref
columns.description: How many cross-reference term copies the run created. Almost never used — 865 of 875 rows are 0, with a maximum of 3.

columns.name: total_verses_inserted
columns.description: How many verse records the run wrote, 0 to 8,044. The single largest measure of a run's effect on the verse tables.

columns.name: total_verses_filtered
columns.description: How many fetched verses the run rejected before storing. Effectively dormant: 859 of 875 rows are 0, so filtering almost never fires.

columns.name: total_meanings_parsed
columns.description: How many meaning blocks the run parsed into the meaning tables. 0 in 511 rows, reflecting the runs that touch no lexical data.

columns.name: error_detail
columns.description: What went wrong, or in some rows what went right. DEFECT of naming: 393 rows are NULL but the populated ones mix genuine errors ('["A1: No wa_file_index rows for registry 213..."]') with success payloads such as '{"vc_updated": 77}', so the column is not purely an error channel and its content is sometimes JSON, sometimes a JSON array of strings.

columns.name: resume_from
columns.description: Intended to let an interrupted run restart from a checkpoint, but NULL in all 875 rows — the resume capability was declared and never used.

engine_stream_checkpoint.description: Per-stream progress within a run (1,948 rows over 347 runs) — a stream is usually a single term, e.g. 'term:H8637'. It exists to allow resumable, granular progress tracking, and in practice 1,938 of 1,948 streams show complete.
engine_stream_checkpoint.sql:
CREATE TABLE engine_stream_checkpoint (
            id               INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            run_id           TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES engine_run_log(run_id),
            stream_name      TEXT    NOT NULL,
            status           TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',
            last_registry_id TEXT,
            last_strong      TEXT,
            rows_written     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            rows_filtered    INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            error_detail     TEXT,
            started_at       TEXT,
            completed_at     TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for one stream's checkpoint.

columns.name: run_id
columns.description: The engine run the stream belongs to. Formats are mixed as in the parent log: mostly 'RUN-{timestamp}-{MODE}', but some are of the form 'vrm_2026-06-10T00:13:42.448Z'.

columns.name: stream_name
columns.description: What the stream processed, most often a single term as 'term:H8637', with a few named streams such as 'FLAG_STREAM'. 276 distinct names across 1,948 rows.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Where the stream got to: 'complete' 1,938, 'review' 6, 'pending' 3, 'running' 1. Lower-case by convention with default 'pending' and no CHECK; the 1 running and 3 pending rows are stale leftovers, not live work.

columns.name: last_registry_id
columns.description: Intended to checkpoint the last registry word processed in the stream, but NULL in all 1,948 rows — declared and never populated.

columns.name: last_strong
columns.description: The last Strong's number the stream reached, e.g. 'G5401', 'H3374'. Populated for only 177 of 1,948 rows, so it checkpoints a small minority of streams.

columns.name: rows_written
columns.description: How many rows the stream wrote, 0 to 14,053. The measure of a stream's actual output.

columns.name: rows_filtered
columns.description: How many rows the stream rejected. Effectively dormant — 1,932 of 1,948 rows are 0.

columns.name: error_detail
columns.description: Despite the name, this carries the stream's summary line rather than errors — e.g. 'verses=64 processed=64 findings=982 audit_flags=35'. Populated for 274 rows; read it as a completion note, not a fault record.

columns.name: started_at
columns.description: When the stream began, ISO-8601 without a zone, 2026-03-18 to 2026-07-13.

columns.name: completed_at
columns.description: When the stream finished. NULL in 335 rows — more unfinished than the 4 non-complete status rows imply, so a stream can be marked complete without a completion time.

finding.description: The universal finding store: one row per typed analytical finding, at VERSE, CLUSTER or GLOBAL level, with VERSE dominating (over 430k of 438k rows). The critical fact in the data is that roughly 92% of rows carry delete_flagged=1 — every l2_api and l2_mechanical row and most l2_meaning rows are soft-deleted, leaving only about 35k live findings; the table is therefore mostly a retained legacy substrate rather than an active corpus.
finding.sql:
CREATE TABLE finding (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            level TEXT NOT NULL,                  -- VERSE | TERM | CLUSTER | GLOBAL
            verse_context_id INTEGER,             -- level=VERSE   -> verse_context.id
            mti_term_id INTEGER,                  -- level=TERM    -> mti_terms.id
            cluster_code TEXT,                    -- level=CLUSTER -> cluster.cluster_code
            finding_value TEXT,
            finding_status TEXT,                  -- ANSWERED|STATED_SILENT|STATED_UNRESOLVED|OPEN|RESOLVED|CLOSED
            provenance TEXT,                      -- mechanical|clarification|api|researcher
            justified_by_finding_id INTEGER,      -- the clarification (higher-level finding) that justifies this
            supersedes_id INTEGER,                -- correction / resolution lineage
            source_legacy_ref TEXT,               -- e.g. wa_session_b_findings.finding_id when migrated
            flagged_for_review INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            created_at TEXT, last_updated_date TEXT,
            delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0
        , characteristic_id INTEGER, cluster_subgroup_id INTEGER, vcg_scope TEXT, notes TEXT, strong_number TEXT)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key for the finding; values run far above the row count (into the millions), so ids are sparse and carry no ordering meaning beyond insertion sequence.

columns.name: level
columns.description: The scope at which the finding is asserted: VERSE (the overwhelming majority), CLUSTER or GLOBAL. Only these three values occur but nothing enforces them — no CHECK or FK backs the column.

columns.name: verse_context_id
columns.description: The classified verse the finding is anchored to, pointing at verse_context. Populated for essentially all VERSE-level rows and left null on the CLUSTER/GLOBAL rows, which have no single verse.

columns.name: mti_term_id
columns.description: The Strong's-level term the finding is about, pointing at mti_terms. Null on the cluster- and global-level rows; on verse rows it identifies which term-in-verse the observation concerns.

columns.name: cluster_code
columns.description: The M-code cluster the finding belongs to (M01, M15, T2 and so on). Roughly a third of rows have no cluster code, and the column is free text with no FK to the cluster table.

columns.name: finding_value
columns.description: The finding itself as prose — the analytical statement about the term in its verse, often several hundred characters of exegetical comment. 672 rows hold an empty string rather than a real statement.

columns.name: finding_status
columns.description: The disposition of the finding: ANSWERED and STATED_SILENT account for almost all verse rows, while cluster/global rows use OPEN, CLOSED, RESOLVED and STATED_UNRESOLVED. Uncontrolled, and the vocabulary is inconsistent — 14 global rows carry lowercase 'active' against otherwise uppercase values.

columns.name: provenance
columns.description: The process that produced the finding — l2_api, l2_mechanical and l2_meaning for the three verse-read generations, plus session_b_migration for the cluster/global rows carried over from Session B, and named runs such as leviticus-lexical-v1 and l2_rollup. It is the key to the table's live/dead split: every l2_api and l2_mechanical row is soft-deleted, and only the l2_meaning, session_b_migration and small named-run rows include live findings.

columns.name: justified_by_finding_id
columns.description: Intended to point at another finding that justifies this one, and indexed for that use, but 100% NULL — declared and never populated across all 438k rows.

columns.name: supersedes_id
columns.description: Points to an earlier finding this row replaces. Used sparingly (a small minority of rows), so revision-by-supersession is the exception rather than the norm.

columns.name: source_legacy_ref
columns.description: Free-text provenance string tying a row back to its pre-migration origin, such as a Session B finding key with its type and registry, or a named run like a verse-narration batch. Only present on migrated rows.

columns.name: flagged_for_review
columns.description: Researcher marker that the finding needs a second look; set on only a handful of rows, the rest defaulting to 0.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When the finding was written. Formats are mixed — some rows hold a bare date, others a full ISO-8601 UTC timestamp — so the column cannot be sorted as a uniform timestamp without normalisation.

columns.name: last_updated_date
columns.description: When the row was last changed. Like created_at the format is inconsistent, mixing space-separated 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' with ISO-8601 UTC.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker. Its distribution is the headline of the table: the great majority of findings are flagged 1, which is how the method reset retired the earlier mechanical and API-generated finding layers without physically deleting them.

finding_citation.description: Extracted citations found inside cluster-level narrative text — the pointer that a given cluster_finding or cluster_observation quotes a particular verse, Strong's number, cross-characteristic or verse-context group. Despite the name it does not cite rows in the finding table; its CHECK constraint binds it to cluster_finding and cluster_observation only, and every row was written in a single batch on 3 June 2026.
finding_citation.sql:
CREATE TABLE "finding_citation" (
            id                INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            source_table      TEXT NOT NULL
                              CHECK (source_table IN ('cluster_finding','cluster_observation')),
            source_id         INTEGER NOT NULL,
            citation_type     TEXT NOT NULL
                              CHECK (citation_type IN ('verse','strongs','cross_char','vcg')),
            citation_value    TEXT NOT NULL,
            position          INTEGER,
            delete_flagged    INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            created_at        TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key; the range starts well above zero, indicating the rows were inserted after earlier ids in the sequence had been consumed.

columns.name: source_table
columns.description: Which narrative table the citation was parsed out of — constrained to cluster_finding or cluster_observation, with cluster_finding supplying the bulk.

columns.name: source_id
columns.description: The row id within source_table that contains the citation; several thousand distinct source rows each contribute multiple citations.

columns.name: citation_type
columns.description: What kind of thing is cited: verse (the large majority), cross_char for a reference to another characteristic, or strongs for a lexical number. The CHECK also permits 'vcg' but no row uses it.

columns.name: citation_value
columns.description: The cited token as it appeared in the text — a verse reference in the programme's abbreviated book form (for example 'Zep 3:5'), a Strong's number, or a characteristic reference.

columns.name: position
columns.description: The character offset of the citation within the source row's text, used to locate and order citations inside the narrative; offsets reach into the tens of thousands for long passages.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker; no row has ever been flagged, so every extracted citation remains live.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: Insertion timestamp. All values fall within a few seconds of one another, confirming the whole table was produced by one extraction run rather than accrued over time.

finding_question_link.description: Joins findings to the observation questions in wa_obs_question_catalogue that they answer — the mechanism by which the question catalogue is scored against the evidence. At 332k rows it is one of the largest tables, but only 31 distinct questions are ever linked, so the link exercises a small fraction of the 424-row catalogue.
finding_question_link.sql:
CREATE TABLE finding_question_link (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            finding_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
            question_id INTEGER NOT NULL,         -- wa_obs_question_catalogue.obs_id
            coverage TEXT,                        -- full | partial | evidence
            created_at TEXT,
            delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0
        , status TEXT, pattern_type TEXT, mapped_date TEXT, validated_date TEXT, validated_by TEXT, session_b_note TEXT, source_legacy_ref TEXT)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key for the link row.

columns.name: finding_id
columns.description: The finding being linked. Values are distinct per row in the profile, so a finding typically answers one catalogued question rather than several.

columns.name: question_id
columns.description: The catalogue question answered, referencing wa_obs_question_catalogue.obs_id. Only 31 questions appear despite 424 existing, and no FK enforces the reference.

columns.name: coverage
columns.description: How fully the finding answers the question. In practice the value tracks the finding's provenance rather than an independent judgement — 'direct' maps one-to-one onto the l2_api findings and 'full' onto the l2_mechanical ones — with 'answers', 'partial' and 'rollup' appearing only a handful of times.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When the link was made; formats are mixed between space-separated and ISO-8601 UTC timestamps.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker; effectively unused, with only a single row flagged.

finding_revision.description: Declared as a field-level audit trail for changes to findings — recording which field moved from what value to what, why, and by whom — but it holds 0 rows. It was created and indexed but never written to, so finding history has no record here.

columns.name: finding_id

columns.name: value_from

columns.name: value_to

finding_verse_link.description: Links findings to the verses they rest on, distinguishing the anchor verse from supporting ones. The table is small and lopsided: 3,586 of 3,659 rows are 'anchor' rows that carry only a textual reference and no verse_record_id, while the 73 'SUPPORT' rows are the only ones actually resolved to a verse record.
finding_verse_link.sql:
CREATE TABLE finding_verse_link (
            id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            finding_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
            verse_record_id INTEGER,              -- wa_verse_records.id (or reference where no row)
            reference TEXT,
            role TEXT,                            -- anchor | evidence
            created_at TEXT,
            delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key for the link row.

columns.name: finding_id
columns.description: The finding the verse supports; 1,446 distinct findings are represented, several citing more than one verse.

columns.name: verse_record_id
columns.description: The resolved wa_verse_records row for the verse. 98% NULL — only the small SUPPORT set was ever resolved to a verse record, so the link is textual rather than relational for almost every row.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: The verse as written text (for example '1 Cor 11:25'). Eight rows hold an em dash instead of a reference, a placeholder standing where no verse was actually cited.

columns.name: role
columns.description: Whether the verse anchors the finding or merely supports it. Values are 'anchor' and 'SUPPORT' — uncontrolled, and inconsistently cased between the two batches that wrote them.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When the link was written; six distinct timestamps show the table is the product of a handful of batch runs, not incremental authoring.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker; ten rows are flagged, the rest live.

ib_characteristic.description: The live meaning-keyed inner-being characteristic index: one row per distinct sense of a Hebrew term as read in a book, keyed on lemma plus English reading rather than on the lemma alone. 1,634 rows, all provenance 'ib-char-index-v3-meaning-keyed-2026' and all status 'surfaced', covering only Psalms (877) and Proverbs (757). Seven columns inherited from the older registry shape are 100% NULL.
ib_characteristic.sql:
CREATE TABLE ib_characteristic (
      id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, code TEXT UNIQUE, name TEXT, aka TEXT, family TEXT,
      status TEXT, books TEXT, gist TEXT, colour_range TEXT, junctions TEXT,
      open_questions TEXT, discovery_doc TEXT, provenance TEXT, created_at TEXT, updated_at TEXT, char_key TEXT, key_word TEXT, key_span_id INTEGER, operation TEXT, ledger TEXT, instance_count INTEGER, book_scope TEXT, stems TEXT, morph_codes TEXT, esv_words TEXT, lexical_gloss TEXT, read_sense_variants TEXT, cluster TEXT, cluster_all TEXT)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key.

columns.name: code
columns.description: The characteristic's unique handle, composed as book-Strong's-word (for example 'psa-H0014-submit'); unique across all 1,634 rows.

columns.name: name
columns.description: The English reading word that keys the sense ('zeal', 'needy one'); 1,099 distinct names, so the same English word recurs against different lemmas.

columns.name: aka
columns.description: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL on all 1,634 rows. Carried over from the legacy registry shape, which did use it.

columns.name: family
columns.description: Groups the characteristic into one of 48 thematic families ('wisdom-folly-teaching', 'desire-longing-appetite', 'inner-seat-heart-soul-spirit'), with 61 parked in 'other-uncategorised'. Convention only, no constraint.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Maturity of the characteristic; every one of the 1,634 rows is 'surfaced' — none has advanced beyond first surfacing.

columns.name: books
columns.description: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL. Superseded by book_scope, which carries the numeric book id instead.

columns.name: gist
columns.description: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL. The legacy registry used this for the one-line law or summary.

columns.name: colour_range
columns.description: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL. In the legacy registry this held how a characteristic changes sense by object.

columns.name: junctions
columns.description: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL. Intended for links to neighbouring characteristics.

columns.name: open_questions
columns.description: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL.

columns.name: discovery_doc
columns.description: Declared but never populated: 100% NULL — these rows were generated by index build, not by discovery documents.

columns.name: provenance
columns.description: The build that produced the row; a single value, 'ib-char-index-v3-meaning-keyed-2026', across the whole table.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: Compact UTC timestamp (YYYYMMDDThhmmssZ, not ISO-8601 with separators like the rest of the schema). Only two values: the 2026-07-11 Psalms build and the 2026-07-14 Proverbs build.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.description: Compact UTC timestamp of the last change; identical to created_at on every row — nothing has been edited since its build.

columns.name: char_key
columns.description: The meaning key in lemma:reading form ('H8668:victory'). 1,455 distinct over 1,634 rows, so the key is not unique — the same lemma-plus-reading recurs across the two books.

columns.name: key_word
columns.description: The reading word of the key; duplicates name on every row.

columns.name: key_span_id
columns.description: The specific span occurrence chosen to anchor this sense, unique per row, pointing at the verse-span layer.

columns.name: operation
columns.description: What the term does in context, phrased as a verbal action ('refuse to submit', 'be needy', 'be defended') — the movement the characteristic performs, which is the study's live analytical object.

ib_observation.description: A small transitional store of 81 observations from the fan-out reads of nine focus verses (chiefly Lev 25:43, Exo 1:13 and Gen 6:5), each tying a dimension to a term anchor with a narrative. Per the method reset these fold into ve_lexical items; the store is not linked to the lexical tables and covers only a handful of verses.
ib_observation.sql:
CREATE TABLE ib_observation(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, operation TEXT, dimension TEXT, narrative TEXT,
  term_anchor TEXT NOT NULL, origin_verse TEXT, origin_verse_id INTEGER,
  reconsider_at TEXT, status TEXT, provenance TEXT, basis TEXT, raw_file TEXT,
  created TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')))

lemma_faculty_map.description: Maps 1,717 Strong's lemmas to the inner-being faculty or faculties they engage (affect, cognition, volition, moral evaluation and combinations), with a stated basis and a confidence. Machine-generated in a single run on 2026-06-24 under model faculty-map-v1: every row shares one model version and one timestamp, so the whole table is one pass with no incremental maintenance since.
lemma_faculty_map.sql:
CREATE TABLE lemma_faculty_map(
       strongs_number TEXT PRIMARY KEY, faculty TEXT, basis TEXT, confidence TEXT,
       model_version TEXT, created_at TEXT)

columns.name: strongs_number
columns.description: The lemma being classified, H/G plus four zero-padded digits, and the primary key — one classification per Strong's.

columns.name: faculty
columns.description: The faculty or faculties the lemma engages, as a comma-joined list (e.g. 'affect,volition'). 815 of 1,717 rows hold an empty string rather than NULL, meaning the run examined the lemma and assigned no faculty; affect is the commonest positive value at 432. Uncontrolled — 36 distinct values with no constraint behind them.

columns.name: basis
columns.description: Free-text justification for the faculty call, typically the gloss plus a short reading of its sense (e.g. 'zealot/zealous — one characterised by burning eager devotion'). Near-unique per row (1,680 distinct of 1,717), so it is genuine per-lemma reasoning rather than boilerplate.

profile.max: zealot/zealous — one characterised by burning eager devotion

columns.name: confidence
columns.description: How firm the faculty call is. Recorded as four values where three were intended: 'high' (882), 'low' (235) and the medium band split across both 'med' (366) and 'medium' (234) — an unenforced vocabulary that must be normalised before the column is aggregated.

columns.name: model_version
columns.description: Identifier of the classifier that produced the row; uniformly 'faculty-map-v1-20260624' across every row, confirming a single unrevised generation.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When the row was written; identical for all 1,717 rows (2026-06-24 12:37:16), so it timestamps the run, not the row.

lexicon.description: A flat reference lexicon of 11,666 Strong's entries harvested wholesale from STEP on 2026-06-16 — original-script lemma, transliteration, gloss, medium definition and corpus occurrence count. It is a background reference covering the whole biblical vocabulary, not just the study's terms, and is independent of mti_terms (which indexes only 4,221 distinct Strong's).
lexicon.sql:
CREATE TABLE lexicon (
            strong            TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            original_unicode  TEXT,
            transliteration   TEXT,
            gloss             TEXT,
            medium_def        TEXT,
            language          TEXT,
            occurrence_count  INTEGER,
            source            TEXT,
            fetched_at        TEXT
        )

columns.name: strong
columns.description: The Strong's number, H/G plus four zero-padded digits, and the primary key — one row per Strong's, with no duplicates across the 11,666 rows.

columns.name: original_unicode
columns.description: The lemma in its own script, Hebrew or Greek (e.g. Ῥώμη, 'Rome'). 11,114 distinct values against 11,666 rows, so a few hundred Strong's entries share a surface form.

columns.name: transliteration
columns.description: Romanised form of the lemma; a reading aid that should never be cited without the gloss beside it.

columns.name: gloss
columns.description: Short English sense of the entry. Only 7,318 distinct values over 11,666 rows — common glosses are shared by many Strong's numbers, so the gloss alone does not identify an entry.

columns.name: medium_def
columns.description: The fuller STEP definition: the substantive lexical content of the row, running from a one-line sense to multi-hundred-character discussions with stem breakdowns and classical notes.

profile.min: (Aphel) to be urgent, harsh, show insolence
profile.max: § to send to hell, hold captive in Tartarus; a derivative of the Greek noun "Tartarus," a place of torture and torment l… (+258 chars)

columns.name: language
columns.description: Language of the entry: Hebrew (7,027), Greek (4,638) and a single Aramaic row. Uncontrolled, and clearly not a real Aramaic classification — the one Aramaic row is the hand-added entry noted in source, so Aramaic lemmas otherwise sit under Hebrew here.

columns.name: occurrence_count
columns.description: How often the lemma occurs in the biblical corpus per STEP. Capped, not exact at the top end: five entries (including G0846 'it/s/he' and G2532 'and') sit at exactly 10000, which is a ceiling rather than a count. Zero is a legitimate value for entries with no attested occurrence.

columns.name: source
columns.description: Where the row came from: 'STEP' for all but one entry, the exception being a manually added Aramaic lemma that STEP returned empty.

columns.name: fetched_at
columns.description: When the entry was retrieved. Effectively a single bulk timestamp of 2026-06-16 for the whole table, plus the one manual row added on 2026-06-26.

mti_term_cross_refs.description: Records the registry words that reference a term other than its owning one — the XREF side of term ownership, held as a junction between mti_terms and word_registry. Small at 462 rows over 279 terms, and skewed to affect vocabulary (wrath, sorrow, terror), so it maps only a fraction of the cross-referencing implied by the ~3,380 XREF rows in wa_term_inventory.
mti_term_cross_refs.sql:
CREATE TABLE "mti_term_cross_refs" (
    id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    mti_term_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES mti_terms(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    registry            TEXT NOT NULL,
    registry_fk         INTEGER REFERENCES word_registry(id),
    word                TEXT,
    part                TEXT,
    word_data_reference TEXT,
    UNIQUE (mti_term_id, registry, word, part)
)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the cross-reference row.

columns.name: mti_term_id
columns.description: The term being cross-referenced, pointing to mti_terms.id; cascades on delete of the term. 279 distinct terms appear, so most cross-referenced terms have only one or two referring registries.

columns.name: registry
columns.description: Registry number of the referring English word, held as text (e.g. '178'). Part of the uniqueness key with mti_term_id, word and part.

columns.name: registry_fk
columns.description: Foreign key to word_registry.id for the referring word. Unlike the equivalent column on mti_terms this one is fully populated, and its 109 distinct values match registry exactly.

columns.name: word
columns.description: The referring English registry word (e.g. 'wrath'), denormalised beside registry; the two columns have identical cardinality, so this is a readability copy.

columns.name: part
columns.description: Which part of a split registry does the referring, where the English word was divided for processing. Set on only 17 rows and written inconsistently as both bare digits and 'Part3'.

columns.name: word_data_reference
columns.description: Pointer to the source Word_Data record that evidenced this cross-reference. Set on only 16 rows, so provenance for this table is effectively absent.

mti_term_flags.description: Junction attaching Phase 2 triage flags from phase2_flag_types to terms in mti_terms; 1,005 assignments across 785 terms. In practice it uses a very narrow slice of the flag vocabulary — 994 of the 1,005 rows are just GOD_AS_SUBJECT and SOMATIC_INNER_LINK.
mti_term_flags.sql:
CREATE TABLE mti_term_flags (
            mti_term_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES mti_terms(id),
            flag_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES phase2_flag_types(id),
            PRIMARY KEY (mti_term_id, flag_id)
        )

columns.name: mti_term_id
columns.description: The flagged term, half of the composite primary key with flag_id. 785 distinct terms carry flags, so most flagged terms hold a single flag.

columns.name: flag_id
columns.description: The flag type applied, pointing to phase2_flag_types.id. Only four types are used here: 1 GOD_AS_SUBJECT (584), 3 SOMATIC_INNER_LINK (410), 13 THEOLOGICAL_ANCHOR (9) and 4 BODY_INNER_EXPRESSION (2).

mti_term_subgroup.description: The many-to-many placement of terms into cluster sub-groups, replacing the old single-valued column on mti_terms. 1,196 placements over 740 distinct terms, so a term can sit in several sub-groups, with the placement note distinguishing primary from secondary. 173 placements are delete-flagged.
mti_term_subgroup.sql:
CREATE TABLE mti_term_subgroup (
            id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            mti_term_id         INTEGER NOT NULL
                                  REFERENCES mti_terms(id),
            cluster_subgroup_id INTEGER NOT NULL
                                  REFERENCES cluster_subgroup(id),
            placement_note      TEXT,
            delete_flagged      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
            last_updated_date   TEXT NOT NULL,
            UNIQUE (mti_term_id, cluster_subgroup_id)
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key; maximum id 1,247 against 1,196 rows, so some placements were hard-deleted.

columns.name: mti_term_id
columns.description: The term being placed; 740 distinct terms, several placed into more than one sub-group.

columns.name: cluster_subgroup_id
columns.description: The sub-group the term is placed into; 160 sub-groups have members, the busiest holding 35 terms.

columns.name: placement_note
columns.description: Why the term sits here, citing the routing directive and marking the placement '[primary]' or '[secondary]' — this text is the only record of primary-versus-secondary status. 243 rows read 'M46 backfill from mti_terms.cluster_subgroup_id', marking the migration off the old single-valued column.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker; 173 of 1,196 placements retired and retained.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: ISO-8601 UTC creation timestamp, in 27 directive-sized batches.

columns.name: last_updated_date
columns.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the last change to the placement.

mti_terms.description: The master term index: one row per Hebrew/Greek/Aramaic term drawn into the study, carrying the term's identity (Strong's, transliteration, gloss, language), which English registry word owns it, its extraction status and its Verse Context progress. Intended as one row per Strong's, but the data does not bear that out: 7,861 rows cover only 4,221 distinct Strong's numbers, and the 5,131 delete-flagged rows still repeat 2,567 Strong's; only the 2,730 live rows are genuinely one-per-Strong's. Extraction dates cluster in March 2026, so the bulk of the table is an early-programme intake that has since been pruned by flagging rather than deletion.
mti_terms.sql:
CREATE TABLE "mti_terms" (
            id                       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            strongs_number           TEXT,
            transliteration          TEXT,
            gloss                    TEXT,
            language                 TEXT,
            owning_registry          TEXT,
            owning_registry_fk       INTEGER REFERENCES word_registry(id),
            owning_word              TEXT,
            owning_part              TEXT,
            word_data_reference      TEXT,
            word_data_ref_fk         INTEGER,
            status                   TEXT,
            exclusion_reason         TEXT,
            extraction_date          TEXT,
            strongs_reconciled       INTEGER,
            anchor_note              TEXT,
            last_changed             TEXT,
            delete_flagged           INTEGER,
            vc_status                TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'not_done',
            vc_instruction_version   TEXT,
            vc_status_updated_at     TEXT,
            vc_status_note           TEXT,
            md_version               INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
            cluster_code             TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the term record; the value referenced as mti_term_id throughout the finding, verse-context and cluster layers.

columns.name: strongs_number
columns.description: The term's Strong's identifier, normally H/G plus four zero-padded digits (e.g. H7965), sometimes with a sub-entry suffix letter. Not clean: six rows hold placeholders such as 'PENDING-135-metameleia' or 'G_PENDING_epelpizo' for terms onboarded before a Strong's was resolved, and one row carries the unpadded 'G194'.

columns.name: transliteration
columns.description: Romanised form of the lemma, used to name the term in prose and reports. Never authoritative on its own — always read with the gloss; a few rows hold only whitespace.

columns.name: gloss
columns.description: Short English sense of the term (e.g. 'zealot'), the working label used when the term is named in analysis. Some values carry a leading space, and proper nouns such as ' Philippi' show that the intake was not filtered to inner-being vocabulary.

columns.name: language
columns.description: Source language of the term: Hebrew (5,457), Greek (2,281) or Aramaic (123). Convention only — no CHECK constraint enforces the three values.

columns.name: owning_registry
columns.description: The registry number of the English word that is this term's canonical home, held as text (e.g. '187'). Legacy text pointer superseded by owning_registry_fk but still the better-populated of the two — only 8 rows are null.

columns.name: owning_registry_fk
columns.description: Proper foreign key to word_registry.id for the owning English word. Populated on only 4,336 of 7,861 rows: 3,522 rows carry an owning_registry text value with no matching FK, so this column is an incomplete migration of that pointer and must not be treated as the sole ownership signal.

columns.name: owning_word
columns.description: The English registry word that owns the term, denormalised alongside owning_registry for readability.

columns.name: owning_part

passage.description: The passage register (4,296 rows): a passage is a maximal run of consecutive verses forming the reading unit, anchored on its first verse. Notably no passage crosses a chapter boundary (start_chapter equals end_chapter on all 4,296 rows), so passages are chapter-bounded in practice. Referenced by verse.passage_id, though no FK is declared in either direction.
passage.sql:
CREATE TABLE passage (
      id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ref TEXT, anchor_verse_id INTEGER,
      book_id INTEGER, start_chapter INTEGER, start_verse INTEGER,
      end_chapter INTEGER, end_verse INTEGER, verse_count INTEGER,
      source TEXT, review_flag TEXT, notes TEXT, created_at TEXT)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key; the target of verse.passage_id. The range runs to 4,401 against 4,296 rows, so about 100 passages have been deleted outright.

columns.name: ref
columns.description: The passage's human reference range, e.g. '1Ch 10:12-14'; unique across the table.

columns.name: anchor_verse_id
columns.description: The verse.id of the passage's first verse — the anchor at which term-driven processing begins. Its range reaches 23,984, exceeding some other tables' verse_id ceilings.

columns.name: book_id
columns.description: Canonical book number; Proverbs (20) has by far the most passages at 701, reflecting its verse-by-verse structure.

columns.name: start_chapter
columns.description: Chapter of the first verse. Identical to end_chapter on every row.

columns.name: start_verse
columns.description: Verse number of the first verse; 684 passages start at verse 1.

columns.name: end_chapter
columns.description: Chapter of the last verse — identical to start_chapter on all 4,296 rows, so it carries no information beyond start_chapter.

columns.name: end_verse
columns.description: Verse number of the last verse in the run.

columns.name: verse_count
columns.description: Number of verses in the passage, 1..39; the commonest are 2 (946) and 1 (642), so passages are typically very short.

columns.name: source
columns.description: How the passage was derived: 'consecutive' (3,579, the standard maximal-run rule), 'passage-build-2026' (701, all Proverbs) and 'single-verse-emergent-char-2026' (16). Convention only, no CHECK.

columns.name: review_flag
columns.description: Present on only the 16 single-verse emergent passages, all holding the string '0'. The declared type is TEXT but the content is a numeric flag, and with a single value it currently marks nothing.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Present on only the same 16 rows, all with the identical text 'single-verse passage: isolated emergent characteristic, no adjacent char-verse' — a rationale for the exception, not a per-row note.

prose_section.description: The DB-canonical store of authored prose: one row per titled section of narrative — chapter readings, cluster essays, synthesis passages and programme documentation — with its full body text, version lineage and approval state. Almost all of it is machine-authored (claude_code or claude_ai); exactly one row is attributed to the researcher.
prose_section.sql:
CREATE TABLE "prose_section" (
            id                INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            registry_id       INTEGER REFERENCES word_registry(id),
            section_type_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES prose_section_type(id),
            heading           TEXT,
            body              TEXT    NOT NULL,
            word_count        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            status            TEXT    NOT NULL,
            version           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
            author            TEXT    NOT NULL,
            created_at        TEXT    NOT NULL,
            approved_at       TEXT,
            approved_by       TEXT,
            metadata_json     TEXT,
            delete_flagged    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, cluster_code TEXT, characteristic_id INTEGER, cluster_subgroup_id INTEGER, updated_at TEXT,
            CHECK (status IN ('draft','in_review','approved','archived')),
            CHECK (author IN ('claude_ai','claude_code','researcher'))
        )

columns.name: body

prose_section_type.description: The controlled vocabulary of prose section kinds — 108 codes spanning programme documentation, per-session outputs, cluster findings and lexical prose — each with a label, the stage that produces it, and expected length bounds. prose_section_type.sql:
CREATE TABLE "prose_section_type" (
                id                   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
                code                 TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
                label                TEXT    NOT NULL,
                source_stage         TEXT    NOT NULL,
                lifecycle_tag        TEXT,
                chapter_no           INTEGER,
                description          TEXT,
                expected_length_min  INTEGER,

                sort_order           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

                book_label           TEXT,

                updated_at           TEXT,
                CHECK (source_stage IN ('programme','session_a','session_b','session_b_phase9','session_c','session_d','synthesis','verse-analysis','findings','essay','contributor')),
                CHECK (lifecycle_tag IS NULL OR lifecycle_tag IN ('source','v1','v2','v3')),
                CHECK (book_label IS NULL OR book_label IN ('Programme','Detail design','Findings','Essays'))
            )

schema_version.description: Migration ledger: one row per schema version applied to the database, each carrying the cumulative migration history as JSON. 16 rows spanning 3.15.0 to later versions, written between April and the present — it is an append-only audit trail, not a single-row current-version marker.
schema_version.sql:
CREATE TABLE "schema_version" (
            id                 INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            version_code       TEXT    NOT NULL,
            applied_at         TEXT    NOT NULL,
            migration_history  TEXT,
            engine_min_version TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key, one per recorded version, 1-16 in application order.

columns.name: version_code
columns.description: The schema version reached, e.g. '3.15.0', '3.16.1', '3.21.0'. Unique per row; the highest value is the live schema version the engine checks against.

columns.name: applied_at
columns.description: When the version was applied. Mostly ISO-8601 with a Z suffix but not uniformly — at least one value ('2026-04-24T14:47:57') omits the zone marker, so parsing must tolerate both.

columns.name: migration_history
columns.description: The full cumulative migration list as a JSON array of {version, description, applied_at} objects, starting at M01 and growing with each row — the later rows exceed 10,000 characters. This duplicates the whole history in every row rather than storing one migration per row.

columns.name: engine_min_version
columns.description: Declared to record a minimum engine version required by the schema, but never populated: NULL in all 16 rows. No engine-compatibility floor is actually enforced through this column.

segment_unit.description: Reading segments above the verse: 877 named units of text (a thread, discourse or scene) each summarised by the characteristics it carries and a gist. Coverage is narrow and uneven — only 22 books appear, with Proverbs (323) and Job (101) dominating — so this is a partially rolled-out layer, not a canon-wide segmentation. 89 rows are soft-deleted.
segment_unit.sql:
CREATE TABLE segment_unit (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  book TEXT, chapter INTEGER,
  unit_code TEXT, unit_type TEXT,        -- D|S|C|T|F

  gist TEXT, verse_ref_summary TEXT,

columns.name: id

term_collection_lexical.description: Holds collection-level lexical judgements about a term — properties asserted of the term across its whole verse set rather than in any one verse (mutability, transitivity, object type, valence register, membership scope, faculty). All 1,081 rows were written mechanically in a single burst on 2026-06-24 under model 01b-PartC-v3, covering 188 terms in six clusters (M12-M20) only.
term_collection_lexical.sql:
CREATE TABLE term_collection_lexical(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  mti_term_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  cluster_code TEXT,
  ve_label TEXT NOT NULL,
  value TEXT,
  derivation TEXT,            -- mechanical | read | researcher
  model_version TEXT,
  source_ref TEXT,            -- evidence summary / source verse(s)
  notes TEXT,
  delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  created_at TEXT
)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key. The range starts at 1036, not 1, so earlier rows of this table were created and removed before the surviving population was written.

columns.name: mti_term_id
columns.description: The term the judgement is about, pointing to mti_terms.id. 188 distinct terms, most carrying the same five or six labels apiece — the population is uniform, not selective.

columns.name: cluster_code
columns.description: The M-code cluster in whose processing the row was generated: M12, M13, M14, M16, M19 and M20 only. Uncontrolled and unlinked to the cluster table, and its narrow span shows this exercise was never rolled out programme-wide.

columns.name: ve_label
columns.description: Which lexical property is being recorded. Five labels are applied uniformly to all 188 terms (membership_scope, mutability, object_type, transitivity, valence_register); faculty_intrinsic covers 88, and valence_discriminator, characteristic_candidate and bivalence_candidate are sparse tails.

columns.name: value
columns.description: The judgement itself, read against the label — e.g. 'intransitive' for transitivity, 'fixed' or 'changeable' for mutability, 'state' for object type. Some values embed their own caveat rather than being a bare token, such as 'present (collection-level; NOT a per-verse seat)'.

columns.name: derivation
columns.description: How the value was arrived at; uniformly 'mechanical' on every row, so no judgement in this table was researcher-authored.

columns.name: model_version
columns.description: The generator that produced the row; uniformly '01b-PartC-v3' across the table.

columns.name: source_ref
columns.description: Evidence trail for the value, often a distribution counted off the term's verses (e.g. a valence tally like {'sinful': 7, 'neutral': 3, 'forbidden': 1}). Some rows carry an empty string, leaving the value unevidenced.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Declared for researcher commentary but never populated — NULL on all 1,081 rows.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker. 0 on every row: nothing in this table has ever been retracted.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When the row was written; nine timestamps all within about ten seconds of each other on 2026-06-24, i.e. a single script run.

term_fetch_log.description: Per-Strong's-number record of STEP API fetches (2,377 rows), showing what was requested, what it resolved to, and how many verses came back and were stored. It is a closed historical log: every row falls between 2026-03-18 and 2026-05-14 and 90 per cent of it belongs to five March bulk gap-fill runs.
term_fetch_log.sql:
CREATE TABLE term_fetch_log (
            id                   INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            run_id               TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES engine_run_log(run_id),
            registry_id          TEXT    NOT NULL,
            strongs_input        TEXT    NOT NULL,
            strongs_resolved     TEXT,
            suffix_resolution    INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            vocab_status         TEXT,
            verse_status         TEXT,
            verse_count_fetched  INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            verse_count_stored   INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            verse_count_filtered INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            span_conflict        INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            api_warnings         TEXT,
            fetched_at           TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for one term fetch.

columns.name: run_id
columns.description: The engine run that made the fetch. Only 20 distinct runs across 2,377 rows, and a single run (RUN-20260318_134133-BULK_GAP_FILL) accounts for 1,170 of them.

columns.name: registry_id
columns.description: The registry word the fetch was for, as TEXT. 148 distinct values, so the log covers about two-thirds of the registry.

columns.name: strongs_input
columns.description: The Strong's number as requested, e.g. 'G0018', 'H8655'. 969 distinct inputs.

columns.name: strongs_resolved
columns.description: The Strong's number the request actually resolved to after suffix handling. 858 distinct values against 969 inputs, so roughly a hundred inputs collapsed onto a shared resolved entry.

columns.name: suffix_resolution
columns.description: Whether resolving the request required handling a sub-entry suffix (e.g. H7965H). Fired for 228 of 2,377 fetches; boolean-by-convention with no CHECK.

columns.name: vocab_status
columns.description: Whether the vocabulary lookup succeeded ('ok', 2,001) or the term was handled as a cross-reference copy ('xref', 376). Two values, uncontrolled.

columns.name: verse_status
columns.description: How the verse fetch ended: 'ok' 1,140, 'pending' 857, 'xref' 376, 'zero_results' 4. Notable that 857 fetches were left pending and never resolved — over a third of the log is unfinished work.

columns.name: verse_count_fetched
columns.description: How many verses STEP returned for the term. The value 480 appears 52 times, which is a suspicious flat repeat and likely reflects the API's paging behaviour rather than 52 terms with identical verse counts.

columns.name: verse_count_stored
columns.description: How many of the fetched verses were written to the database. Its distribution is identical to verse_count_fetched at every value, so nothing was ever dropped between fetch and store and the two columns are redundant.

columns.name: verse_count_filtered
columns.description: How many fetched verses were filtered out before storing. 0 in all 2,377 rows — the filter never once rejected a verse, which is why fetched and stored counts agree exactly.

columns.name: span_conflict
columns.description: Intended to flag a clash in the term's span match within a verse. 0 in all 2,377 rows — the condition was never detected, so the column carries no information.

columns.name: api_warnings
columns.description: Intended to capture warnings returned by the STEP API, but NULL in all 2,377 rows — declared and never populated.

columns.name: fetched_at
columns.description: When the fetch ran, 2026-03-18 to 2026-05-14. The log has been dormant since May.

ve_dimension_scoreboard.description: The rule-validation scoreboard for the 18 VE-lexical dimensions (ve_nr 101-118), holding each dimension's rule, its validation verdict and the first verse where it broke. As of the single 2026-07-14 update no dimension has passed: 8 are FAILED and 10 IN-PROGRESS — this table is the record of the lexical layer failing rule-validation.
ve_dimension_scoreboard.sql:
CREATE TABLE ve_dimension_scoreboard(
  ve_nr INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, dim TEXT, rule TEXT, status TEXT, checked INTEGER,
  first_error_ref TEXT, note TEXT, updated_at TEXT)

columns.name: ve_nr
columns.description: The dimension number and primary key, 101-118 with no gaps. Note the range extends to 117 (device) and 118 (direction), two beyond the 101-116 list given in the project reference.

columns.name: dim
columns.description: The dimension's name — sense, type, source, seat, bearer, operation, target, manner, intensity, specifier, effect, coupling, prohibition, reading, role, locus, device, direction — one each, unique.

columns.name: rule
columns.description: The extraction rule the dimension is supposed to follow, stated compactly and typed as PAIR, EVENT or FLAG (for example 'PAIR term->object (+object-type)'). This is the specification the validation checks against.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Validation verdict: FAILED on 8 dimensions and IN-PROGRESS on 10. No dimension carries a PASS — the notable fact about this table.

columns.name: checked
columns.description: How many instances of the dimension were checked to reach the verdict; between 4 and 12, and the notes make clear these are small samples short of the intended full run.

columns.name: first_error_ref
columns.description: The first verse reference where the dimension's rule broke ('Pro 16:9', 'Pro 21:30'); NULL on the 10 dimensions with no error found yet. All errors so far are in Proverbs.

columns.name: note
columns.description: The validator's reasoning — what was clean, what drifted, what still needs a full check. Carries the substance of the verdict that status only summarises.

ve_lexical.description: The live lexical-analysis store: one row per analytical item read off a verse, keyed to a verse span and a dimension number (ve_nr 101-118 for the verse-level dimensions, 201-211 for a smaller second band). 620,151 rows, all created between 2026-07-02 and 2026-07-14, with ids starting at 7123085 — exactly where ve_lexical_legacy stops, so the two tables are disjoint generations of the same store, cut over on 2026-07-02.
ve_lexical.sql:
CREATE TABLE ve_lexical (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  verse_context_id INTEGER REFERENCES verse_context(id),
  verse_span_id INTEGER REFERENCES verse_span_index(id),
  gate TEXT,
  ve_nr INTEGER, ve_label TEXT, related_tier TEXT, value TEXT, notes TEXT,
  source_provenance TEXT, delete_flagged INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at TEXT,
  from_span TEXT, to_span TEXT, direction TEXT, resolution TEXT, pair_kind TEXT)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the item. Its range (7123085 upward) continues the sequence used by ve_lexical_legacy, so ids are unique across both generations and can be traced between them.

columns.name: verse_context_id
columns.description: Legacy anchor to the verse_context row. 461,208 of 620,151 rows leave it NULL: the live build anchors on verse_span_id instead, and this column survives mainly on rows carried over from the older verse-context-keyed model.

columns.name: verse_span_id
columns.description: The authoritative anchor: the verse span (word/sense occurrence) the item was read from. Populated on all but 322 rows.

columns.name: gate
columns.description: Marks how central the item is to the read, using two values, 1-primary and 2-relevant; 125,070 rows are NULL. Uncontrolled vocabulary — no CHECK or lookup enforces the pair.

columns.name: ve_nr
columns.description: The dimension number the item belongs to. 29 values in use: a main band 101-118 (sense, type, source, seat, bearer, operation, target, manner, intensity, specifier, effect, coupling, prohibition, discovery, role, locus, device, direction) and a sparser band 201-211. Uncontrolled — the catalogue that defines these numbers is not enforced in the database.

columns.name: ve_label
columns.description: The dimension's name, paired one-to-one with ve_nr. Denormalised for readability; nothing in the schema guarantees the pairing stays consistent.

columns.name: related_tier
columns.description: Wholly NULL across all 620,151 rows. The tier scheme this carried in the legacy generation was dropped at the 2026-07-02 cutover; the column is retained but dead.

columns.name: value
columns.description: The finding itself — the analytical content read from the verse for this dimension. Free prose ranging from a single gloss to a sentence of exegesis; the substance of the table.

profile.min: 'ANGUISH (chil) as of a woman in labour' — writhing distress imaged as birth-pangs; chil the labouring agony that convul… (+80 chars)
profile.max: zur (strange/forbidden) — 'the MOUTH of forbidden women is a deep pit'; the seductress's flattering speech is a deadly t… (+80 chars)

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Optional qualifying remark on the item. Populated on a small minority of rows and used inconsistently.

profile.max: zimmah = taking a woman and her daughter is DEPRAVITY/lewdness

columns.name: source_provenance
columns.description: Which read or process produced the item. Seven values, dominated by lexical-model-2026 (474,019), then the per-book re-reads reread-psalms-2026, reread-proverbs-2026, leviticus-lexical-v1, plus role-reassess-2026 and locus-derivation-v1-20260704. Uncontrolled vocabulary — the essential handle for isolating or reversing a given run.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker; withdrawn items stay in place with 1 rather than being removed. A substantial share of rows carry it.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: ISO timestamp of insertion. Spans 2026-07-02 to 2026-07-14 only, so it dates the run rather than the reading.

columns.name: from_span
columns.description: The originating side of a paired item. Nominally a span reference but in practice mixed: only 5,851 of 74,419 populated values are numeric ids, the rest being lemmas or English words — so it cannot be relied on as a foreign key.

columns.name: to_span
columns.description: The receiving side of a paired item. Same mixed content as from_span: 16,047 of 95,881 populated values are numeric, the remainder lemmas or Strong's numbers such as H8668.

columns.name: direction
columns.description: Orientation of a paired or event item. Overwhelmingly the single value 1to2 (68,568), but the column is contaminated: a tail of roughly 300 distinct values holds truncated prose fragments (for example 'static — 29:22).') that are plainly commentary spilled into the wrong field.

profile.max: toward-god — zamar here the song of the one who trusts the Judg

columns.name: resolution
columns.description: How the item's counterpart was settled — span (resolved to a span), inferred, none, or value. NULL on 498,373 rows, i.e. only pair-like items use it. Uncontrolled vocabulary.

columns.name: pair_kind
columns.description: The item's shape: value (a plain reading, 397,222), pair, event, flag, or note. This is what distinguishes a simple dimension value from a relation, an occurrence, or a marker. Uncontrolled vocabulary.

ve_lexical_verification.description: A small manual verification log: 46 hand-checked ve_lexical items, all of dimension 101 (sense) and all checked on 2026-07-14, recording whether the stored reading was right. CREATE TABLE ve_lexical_verification (

  verse_span_id INTEGER NOT NULL,
  ve_nr INTEGER NOT NULL,

Capped at 200 items per dimension — 16 dimensions hit the cap, while 103 yielded 123 and 113 only 9, so those two are under-sampled by availability rather than by design.
ve_verification_sample.sql:
CREATE TABLE ve_verification_sample(
  ve_nr INTEGER, verse_span_id INTEGER, book_id INTEGER, seq INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY(ve_nr, verse_span_id))

columns.name: ve_nr
columns.description: The dimension the sampled item belongs to, part of the composite key. Covers 101-118 only; the 201-211 band is not sampled.

columns.name: verse_span_id
columns.description: The sampled span, part of the composite key. A few spans appear under more than one dimension.

verse.description: The master verse table and the anchor of the whole verse layer: one row per verse of the ESV text (25,634 rows, all 66 books), each with its text, canonical identifiers and the passage/genre/process fields that drive the reading method. Every other verse-layer table keys back to verse.id.
verse.sql:
CREATE TABLE verse (
            id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            osis_id     TEXT UNIQUE,
            reference   TEXT UNIQUE,
            book_id     INTEGER,
            chapter     INTEGER,
            verse_num   INTEGER,
            testament   TEXT,
            verse_text  TEXT,
            created_at  TEXT
        , passage_id INTEGER, is_passage_anchor INTEGER, process_marker TEXT, genre TEXT)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate verse key, dense 1..25634 with no gaps; the join target for verse_morphology, verse_span_index, passage and the verse_id columns across the layer.

columns.name: osis_id
columns.description: OSIS-style reference such as '1Chr.10.1' — the machine/interchange form of the reference, unique per verse and the alternate key to the human form in reference.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: The programme's canonical human reference, e.g. '1Ch 10:1' (three-letter book abbreviation, space, chapter:verse). This is the string other tables carry denormalised; unique across the table.

columns.name: book_id
columns.description: Canonical book number 1..66 (66 distinct present), joining to books; Psalms (19) is the largest at 2,461 verses.

columns.name: chapter
columns.description: Chapter number within the book, 1..150 (150 being the Psalms ceiling).

columns.name: verse_num
columns.description: Verse number within the chapter; 176 distinct values, the maximum reflecting Psalm 119.

columns.name: testament
columns.description: 'OT' (20,015) or 'NT' (5,619). A two-value convention with no CHECK constraint behind it (UNCONTROLLED-VOCAB).

columns.name: verse_text
columns.description: The full ESV verse text. Note the stored text is prefixed with the reference itself (e.g. '1Ch 10:1 Now the Philistines...'), so it is not clean text — consumers must strip the prefix.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the row's ingestion; the values span 2026-06-16 to 2026-07-05, i.e. the master verse table was built in a single recent campaign.

columns.name: passage_id
columns.description: The passage this verse belongs to, pointing at passage.id; 3,255 verses (13%) have no passage, so passage cover of the canon is incomplete. No FK is declared despite the passage table existing.

columns.name: is_passage_anchor
columns.description: 1 on the first verse of its passage (4,296 anchors — exactly the passage row count), 0 otherwise; 3,317 rows are NULL, tracking the unassigned verses.

columns.name: process_marker
columns.description: Free-text stamp recording which reading/lexical run last processed this verse, e.g. 'reread-psalms-2026' (2,420 verses) or 'Lam-3-poetic-lexical-20260703'. 15,454 verses (60%) are unmarked, so this is a progress ledger of what has been read, not a complete field.

columns.name: genre
columns.description: The verse's genre band driving genre-aware reading: 'prophetic', 'law/narrative', 'narrative', 'poetic/wisdom', 'epistle', 'gospel-narrative'. Populated for every verse but enforced only by convention (UNCONTROLLED-VOCAB).
