verse_context.description: The term-in-verse classification record (55,775 rows): for one verse-record and one MTI term it holds whether that occurrence is relevant to the study, which verse-context group and cluster subgroup it belongs to, and the L1/L2 verse-read fields (keywords, analysis note, meaning). Unique on (verse_record_id, mti_term_id, group_id, cluster_subgroup_id). Several columns declared for a sense/pole model were never populated.
verse_context.sql:
CREATE TABLE "verse_context" (
            id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            verse_record_id     INTEGER NOT NULL
                                  REFERENCES wa_verse_records(id),
            mti_term_id         INTEGER NOT NULL
                                  REFERENCES mti_terms(id),
            group_id            INTEGER REFERENCES verse_context_group(id),
            cluster_subgroup_id INTEGER REFERENCES cluster_subgroup(id),
            is_anchor           INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            is_relevant         INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            is_related          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            notes               TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
            delete_flagged      INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            set_aside_reason    TEXT DEFAULT NULL,
            analysis_note       TEXT, keywords TEXT, step_meaning_applied TEXT, sense_id INTEGER, sense_multiplicity TEXT, step_envelope_note TEXT, pole TEXT, pole_is_metaphor INTEGER DEFAULT 0, residue_flag INTEGER DEFAULT 0, thing_type TEXT, triage_status TEXT, meaning_provenance TEXT, flagged_for_review INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            UNIQUE (verse_record_id, mti_term_id, group_id,
                    cluster_subgroup_id)
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key.

columns.name: verse_record_id
columns.description: The wa_verse_records occurrence being classified; the anchor of the row to a specific term-in-verse.

columns.name: mti_term_id
columns.description: The Strong's-level term (mti_terms) the classification is about. Shared across OWNER and XREF copies of a term, so one context row can serve both.

columns.name: group_id
columns.description: The verse_context_group this occurrence was placed in; NULL for a large share of rows (roughly a third of the sample), i.e. grouping is partial.

columns.name: cluster_subgroup_id
columns.description: The cluster subgroup assignment for this occurrence; heavily NULL (about three-quarters of the sample), so subgroup placement covers only part of the classified set.

columns.name: is_anchor
columns.description: 1 marks this occurrence as the anchor/exemplar verse for its grouping. Convention only, no CHECK.

columns.name: is_relevant
columns.description: 1 = this term's use in this verse is in scope for the inner-being study, 0 = judged out of scope. The primary in/out gate of the layer.

columns.name: is_related
columns.description: 1 = the occurrence is related to the study concern rather than a direct instance; a softer secondary marker sitting alongside is_relevant.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-text working note on the classification, frequently carrying directive identifiers (e.g. 'DIR-20260516-003 ... dual-membership') that record why the row was changed. Populated on a small minority of rows.

columns.name: set_aside_reason
columns.description: The prose justification for setting an occurrence aside as out of scope (e.g. a term used in a literal physical rather than inner-being sense). Present only where an exclusion was argued.

columns.name: step_meaning_applied
columns.description: The STEP lexicon gloss/meaning selected as applying to this occurrence. Note it includes empty strings as well as NULLs, so 'unset' is recorded two different ways.

verse_coverage.description: A derived, materialised roll-up of study coverage per verse — how many spans, study terms and lexical units each verse carries, and whether it is in scope. It is a stale snapshot: all 23,593 rows were built at one instant on 2026-06-27 and it covers verse_id 1..23593 only, so 2,041 of the master table's 25,634 verses are absent. The scope_basis column itself declares the underlying anchor 'debunked'.
verse_coverage.sql:
CREATE TABLE verse_coverage (
  verse_id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  reference       TEXT,
  testament       TEXT,
  n_spans         INTEGER,
  n_study_nonT2   INTEGER,
  n_T2            INTEGER,
  scope           TEXT,      -- in-scope | T2-only | no-study  (PROVISIONAL: cluster-based)
  n_lexical_units INTEGER,   -- active ve_lexical units on non-T2 terms
  touched         INTEGER,   -- 1/0
  scope_basis     TEXT DEFAULT 'provisional: mti cluster_code (non-T2 study term) — debunked anchor; recomputable',
  built_at        TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
)

columns.name: verse_id
columns.description: The verse this roll-up describes (also the primary key); ranges 1..23593, short of the master verse table's 25,634 — the snapshot predates later verses.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: The verse reference, denormalised from verse for readability.

columns.name: testament
columns.description: 'OT' (17,974) or 'NT' (5,619), copied from verse; the OT count is 2,041 short of the master table, which is where the whole snapshot's shortfall sits.

columns.name: n_spans
columns.description: Count of morphological spans (words) in the verse; 40 distinct values observed, commonly 7-13.

columns.name: n_study_nonT2
columns.description: Count of spans in the verse carrying a study term that is not a T2 (qualifier-tier) term — the measure of substantive study presence. 3,417 verses have none.

columns.name: n_T2
columns.description: Count of spans carrying a T2 (qualifier/reference-tier) term. 2,639 verses have none.

columns.name: scope
columns.description: The verse's derived scope band: 'in-scope' (20,176), 'T2-only' (3,346, i.e. only qualifier terms present) or 'no-study' (71). Convention only, no CHECK.

columns.name: n_lexical_units
columns.description: Count of lexical units recorded against the verse; 6,699 verses have zero, which is exactly the set with touched=0.

columns.name: touched
columns.description: 1 = some lexical work exists on the verse (16,894), 0 = none (6,699). Derived from n_lexical_units>0, so it duplicates that column's information.

columns.name: scope_basis
columns.default: 'provisional: mti cluster_code (non-T2 study term) — debunked anchor; recomputable'

verse_coverage_morphology.description: A per-word morphology extract for a narrow set of verses — 2,877 word rows covering only 326 distinct references, concentrated in Leviticus, Proverbs and Galatians. It duplicates the shape of verse_morphology on a tiny subset, so it reads as a pilot or one-off working extract from a batch of runs on 2026-06-28 rather than a maintained table.
verse_coverage_morphology.sql:
CREATE TABLE verse_coverage_morphology(
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, reference TEXT, word_index INTEGER, surface TEXT,
  strongs TEXT, primary_strong TEXT, morph_code TEXT, built_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')))

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: The verse reference in programme form; only 326 distinct verses are present, keyed by string rather than by verse.id (no FK to verse).

columns.name: word_index
columns.description: The word's position within the verse, 1..24 here; note it starts at 1, whereas verse_morphology's equivalent starts at 0.

columns.name: surface
columns.description: The surface English word form as rendered by STEP.

columns.name: strongs
columns.description: The raw Strong's tag(s) as delivered for the span, which may include suffixed sub-entry forms.

columns.name: primary_strong
columns.description: The single resolved Strong's number for the span (e.g. 'G0011', 'H8672'); NULL on 75 rows where no head Strong's could be resolved.

columns.name: morph_code
columns.description: The morphology tag for the word — the linguistic source of truth from which language and stem derive; 766 distinct codes across this small extract.

columns.name: built_at
columns.description: Build timestamp; all ten distinct values fall within 2026-06-28, confirming a single-day construction.

verse_evidence_index.description: The fan-in index that answers 'what evidence is bound to this verse' — 804,805 rows mapping a verse to each piece of evidence held against it, so a verse's full raw data can be retrieved in one query. It is a derived index over the other stores, not an authoring surface.
verse_evidence_index.sql:
CREATE TABLE verse_evidence_index(
        verse_id INTEGER, evidence_type TEXT, evidence_id INTEGER, bind_path TEXT, confidence TEXT)

columns.name: verse_id
columns.description: The verse the evidence is bound to; the primary lookup key.

columns.name: evidence_type
columns.description: Which store the evidence lives in: 'lexical' (423,968), 'span' (305,961), 'unit' (42,871) and 'finding_verse' (32,005). A four-value convention with no CHECK or FK — the polymorphic discriminator for evidence_id.

columns.name: evidence_id
columns.description: The row id in the store named by evidence_type. Being polymorphic it can carry no foreign key, so referential integrity here rests entirely on the build process.

columns.name: bind_path
columns.description: How the binding was derived: 'direct:vc-vr' (via verse_context to verse_record), 'direct:morphology' (via the morphology span) or 'direct:verse_record'. It records the provenance of the link, and maps one-to-one onto evidence_type.

columns.name: confidence
columns.description: 'direct' on all 804,805 rows. The column was clearly built to admit indirect/inferred bindings but only direct ones were ever indexed, so it currently carries no information.

verse_evidence_orphan.description: The reject log of the verse_evidence_index build: 222 evidence rows that could not be bound to a verse. Every row has the same single cause, making this a small, specific integrity backlog rather than a general error table.
verse_evidence_orphan.sql: CREATE TABLE verse_evidence_orphan(evidence_type TEXT, evidence_id INTEGER, reason TEXT)

columns.name: evidence_type
columns.description: The store the unbindable evidence came from; 'unit' on all 222 rows, so the failure is confined to segment/verse-record units.

columns.name: evidence_id
columns.description: The id of the evidence row that could not be bound, in the store named by evidence_type.

columns.name: reason
columns.description: The binding failure cause, identical on all 222 rows: 'verse_record has no verse_id'. These are wa_verse_records rows lacking a verse.id link — a concrete, fixable integrity gap.

verse_morph_complexity.description: A derived per-verse syntactic complexity profile counting content words, finite and non-finite verbs, conjunctions, prepositions and subordinators, with a summary score. Like verse_coverage it is a frozen snapshot — all 23,593 rows share one build timestamp of 2026-06-27 and cover verse_id 1..23593, i.e. 2,041 verses short of the master table.
verse_morph_complexity.sql:
CREATE TABLE verse_morph_complexity (
  verse_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, reference TEXT,
  n_content INTEGER, n_finite_verb INTEGER, n_nonfinite_verb INTEGER,
  n_conj INTEGER, n_prep INTEGER, n_subord INTEGER,
  complexity_score INTEGER,
  built_at TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
)

columns.name: verse_id
columns.description: The verse profiled (also the primary key); range 1..23593, short of the master verse table.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: The verse reference, denormalised from verse.

columns.name: n_content
columns.description: Count of content words (as opposed to function words) in the verse; typically 6-11.

columns.name: n_finite_verb
columns.description: Count of finite verbs, derived from morph_code; 2,237 verses have none.

columns.name: n_nonfinite_verb
columns.description: Count of non-finite verb forms (participles, infinitives); 9,656 verses have none.

columns.name: n_conj
columns.description: Count of conjunctions; zero for 18,169 verses, which is high enough to suggest the classifier does not catch prefixed Hebrew conjunctions.

columns.name: n_prep
columns.description: Count of prepositions; zero for 9,502 verses.

columns.name: n_subord
columns.description: Count of subordinating elements, 0..6; zero for 16,647 verses — the sparsest of the counts.

columns.name: complexity_score
columns.description: The composite complexity figure derived from the counts above, 52 distinct values. The weighting formula is not recorded in the data.

columns.name: built_at
columns.description: Build timestamp, identical ('2026-06-27 06:10:51') on all 23,593 rows — a one-shot snapshot never refreshed.

verse_morphology.description: The morphological backbone of the layer: one row per word of every verse (325,507 rows), carrying the surface form, Strong's tag, morph_code and the language/pos/stem derived from it. Unique on (verse_id, word_index) and sourced entirely from STEP. verse_span_index is a near-identical copy of this table plus analytical columns.
verse_morphology.sql:
CREATE TABLE verse_morphology (
            id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            verse_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES verse(id),
            word_index     INTEGER NOT NULL,
            surface        TEXT,
            strongs        TEXT,
            primary_strong TEXT,
            morph_code     TEXT,
            language       TEXT,
            pos            TEXT,
            stem           TEXT,
            person         INTEGER,
            source         TEXT,
            fetched_at     TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key for the word occurrence.

columns.name: verse_id
columns.description: The verse the word belongs to, FK to verse; combined with word_index it uniquely identifies the span.

columns.name: word_index
columns.description: The word's position within the verse, zero-based here (0 appears in the profile) and running to at least 39.

columns.name: surface
columns.description: The surface English word form from STEP. Empty strings occur, so 'no surface' is recorded as '' rather than NULL.

columns.name: strongs
columns.description: The raw Strong's tag(s) for the word as delivered, including suffixed sub-entry forms such as 'G0001G'; nearly 15,000 distinct raw values in the sample against far fewer resolved heads.

columns.name: primary_strong
columns.description: The resolved head Strong's number (zero-padded four digits, H/G prefixed) — the join key to term tables and the indexed lookup here.

columns.name: morph_code
columns.description: The STEP morphology tag and the declared linguistic source of truth for the word. Contamination is visible: some values carry an 'n/a ' prefix (e.g. 'n/a V-PAP-DSM'), so the field is not uniformly clean.

columns.name: language
columns.description: Derived from morph_code: 'Hebrew', 'Greek', 'Aramaic', plus a handful of 'Unknown' where derivation failed. Convention only, no CHECK.

columns.name: pos
columns.description: Part of speech derived from morph_code — 13 distinct values, dominated by noun and verb.

columns.name: stem
columns.description: The Hebrew verbal stem derived from morph_code (Qal, Hiphil, Piel, Niphal, Hithpael and so on). Non-verbs and Greek words carry an empty string rather than NULL, which is why '' is the commonest value.

columns.name: person
columns.description: Grammatical person 1, 2 or 3 where the morph_code encodes it; NULL for the majority of words, which have no person.

columns.name: source
columns.description: 'STEP' on every row — the table has one provenance, so the column currently distinguishes nothing.

columns.name: fetched_at
columns.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the STEP fetch; values run 2026-06-16 to 2026-07-05, matching the verse table's build window.

verse_morphology_raw.description: The raw STEP HTML behind the parsed morphology — one row per verse (25,634, i.e. complete cover of the master verse table), kept so the parse in verse_morphology can be re-derived or audited without re-fetching. This is an archival payload store, not a query surface.
verse_morphology_raw.sql:
CREATE TABLE verse_morphology_raw (
            verse_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES verse(id),
            html        TEXT,
            fetched_at  TEXT
        )

columns.name: verse_id
columns.description: The verse whose raw fetch this is; primary key and FK to verse, one row per verse with no gaps.

columns.name: html
columns.description: The unparsed STEP passage HTML for the verse, roughly 1kB+ per row. It is the provenance record for verse_morphology and is not intended to be read structurally in SQL.

columns.name: fetched_at
columns.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the fetch, spanning 2026-06-16 to 2026-07-05 in step with verse.created_at.

verse_span_index.description: The working analytical surface over word spans (325,474 rows): it reproduces verse_morphology's columns almost exactly and adds the analytical overlay — role, characteristic candidacy, ib_char link and cluster. The duplication is substantial and worth noting: source='verse_morphology' on every row confirms it is a materialised copy, and its row count sits 33 short of the source, so the two can drift.
verse_span_index.sql:
CREATE TABLE verse_span_index (
  id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  -- verse
  verse_id       INTEGER,
  reference      TEXT,
  -- span
  word_index     INTEGER,
  surface        TEXT,
  pos            TEXT,
  morph_code     TEXT,
  stem           TEXT,
  language       TEXT,
  -- term
  strongs        TEXT,
  primary_strong TEXT,
  source         TEXT DEFAULT 'verse_morphology',
  built_at       TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
, role TEXT, role_provenance TEXT, role_set_at TEXT, role_source_ve_id INTEGER, char_candidate INTEGER, char_candidate_tag TEXT, characteristic TEXT, ib_char_id INTEGER, cluster TEXT)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key for the span row (not the same key space as verse_morphology.id despite the copy relationship).

columns.name: verse_id
columns.description: The verse the span sits in; the main lookup key. No FK is declared even though verse_morphology declares one.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: The verse reference, denormalised from verse for direct readability without a join.

columns.name: word_index
columns.description: The word's position in the verse, copied from verse_morphology.

columns.name: surface
columns.description: The surface word form, copied from verse_morphology; empty strings occur.

columns.name: pos
columns.description: Part of speech, copied from verse_morphology (13 distinct values).

columns.name: morph_code
columns.description: The morphology tag copied from verse_morphology, including the same 'n/a ' prefixed contamination.

columns.name: stem
columns.description: Hebrew verbal stem copied from verse_morphology; empty string for non-verbs.

columns.name: language
columns.description: 'Hebrew', 'Greek', 'Aramaic' or 'Unknown', copied from verse_morphology.

columns.name: strongs
columns.description: The raw Strong's tag(s) copied from verse_morphology.

columns.name: primary_strong
columns.description: The resolved head Strong's number; indexed with verse_id, making (verse_id, primary_strong) the intended access path for finding a term's spans in a verse.

columns.name: source
columns.description: 'verse_morphology' on all rows — an explicit statement that this table is a derived copy of that one.

columns.name: built_at
columns.description: Timestamp of the row's build, spanning 2026-06-26 to 2026-07-05; unlike the coverage snapshots this table has been rebuilt incrementally.

columns.name: role
columns.description: The analytical role the span plays in the inner-being model: chiefly 'standalone' (63,719), 'characteristic' (13,514), 'process-qualifier' (7,155) and 'qualifier' (3,168), with a long tail of book-specific values such as 'ritual-mechanical' and 'mistag-not-ib'. Only 27% of spans have a role; the vocabulary is convention with no CHECK, and the tail suggests ad-hoc additions.

columns.name: role_provenance
columns.description: Which campaign assigned the role — 'lexical-model-2026', 'read-2026', 'role-reassess-2026', 'leviticus-lexical-v1' and so on. One sampled row carries the literal value 'CONFLICT', recording an unresolved disagreement between assignments.

columns.name: role_set_at
columns.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp the role was set, 2026-07-07 to 2026-07-14 — role assignment is recent and ongoing.

columns.name: role_source_ve_id
columns.description: The ve_lexical item whose reading produced the role, providing traceability from a role back to the evidence for it. No FK declared.

columns.name: char_candidate
columns.description: 1 marks the span as a candidate inner-being characteristic (30,882 rows); a single row holds 0 and the rest are NULL, so this is effectively a set-membership marker where NULL means 'not a candidate'. Per the project invariant, a char_candidate span with no verse record is an integrity violation.

columns.name: char_candidate_tag
columns.description: The label of the candidate, mostly in an 'IB:<gloss>' form (e.g. 'IB:be gracious'); some values instead record the campaign that raised it ('orphan-reread-2026'), so the field mixes identity and provenance.

columns.name: characteristic
columns.description: The free-text characteristic name attached to the span, keyed on meaning-in-context and often quoting the verse itself (e.g. 'your hand was heavy on me'). Populated on only about 1% of spans.

profile.max: your hand was heavy on me

columns.name: ib_char_id
columns.description: The ib_characteristic this span resolves to — the structured counterpart of the characteristic text column, and populated on exactly the same rows.

columns.name: cluster
columns.description: The M-code cluster (e.g. 'M47', 'M15') the span belongs to; present on well under 1% of spans, so cluster attribution at span level is barely populated.

verse_term_index.description: A minimal derived lookup of which Strong's terms appear in which verse (275,593 rows, no primary key, indexed both ways). It is a de-duplicated projection of verse_morphology's (verse_id, primary_strong) pairs — a fast reverse index for 'which verses contain this term', holding no data of its own.
verse_term_index.sql: CREATE TABLE verse_term_index(verse_id INTEGER, primary_strong TEXT)

columns.name: verse_id
columns.description: The verse containing the term; 23,405 distinct verses in the sample, and its ceiling of 23,593 matches the coverage snapshots rather than the full 25,634-verse master, suggesting it was built in the same earlier campaign.

columns.name: primary_strong
columns.description: The resolved head Strong's number present in that verse; indexed, and the point of the table.

wa_addendum_registry.description: A one-off audit artefact: 22 observations from the April 2026 global-rules audit, each recording a problem with a rule and where its content should migrate. Entirely historical — all 22 rows are marked obsolete with an identical reason, yet all 22 still show migration_status 'pending', so the record contradicts itself.
wa_addendum_registry.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_addendum_registry (
            id                INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            item_id           TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
            addendum_group    TEXT    NOT NULL,
            rule_id           TEXT,
            audit_source      TEXT,
            subject           TEXT,
            observation       TEXT,
            migration_target  TEXT,
            migration_status  TEXT,
            researcher_comment TEXT,
            source_document   TEXT,
            created_at        TEXT    NOT NULL
        , obsolete INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, obsolete_reason TEXT, last_modified TEXT)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the observation, 1-22.

columns.name: item_id
columns.description: The observation's identifier, e.g. 'ADD-INSTR-001'. Unique, and the token cited when an addendum item is referenced.

columns.name: addendum_group
columns.description: Which addendum the item belongs to: 'addendum_instructions' 10, 'addendum_patch_directive' 9, 'addendum_reference' 3. Indexed but uncontrolled.

columns.name: rule_id
columns.description: The wa_rule_registry rule the observation concerns, e.g. 'GR-DATA-001'. A text pointer rather than an FK; 20 of 22 rows name a rule, 2 are NULL.

columns.name: audit_source
columns.description: Where the observation came from — an audit document section or a dated researcher directive, e.g. 'wa-global-rules-audit-v1-20260417.md §2; §6' (8 rows). The provenance of the finding.

wa_cross_registry_links.description: 158 researcher-authored links between registry words, each naming the connecting Hebrew or Greek term and explaining the connection in prose — the pre-cluster way of recording that, say, anguish and grief share vocabulary. Superseded by the cluster model but retained; 140 of the 158 rows date from a single 2026-03-16 load and only 6 have been touched since.
wa_cross_registry_links.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_cross_registry_links (
            id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            file_id             INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_file_index(id),
            linked_word         TEXT,
            linked_registry_id  INTEGER REFERENCES word_registry(id),
            connection_type_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_crosslink_type(id),
            connecting_term     TEXT,
            note                TEXT,
            last_changed        TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the link, 1-158.

columns.name: file_id
columns.description: The wa_file_index entry the link was asserted from — the file whose analysis surfaced the connection. Only 43 distinct files account for all 158 links.

columns.name: linked_word
columns.description: The English registry word being linked to, e.g. 'anguish' (16), 'anger' (13), 'grief' (12). A text copy that duplicates what linked_registry_id resolves to.

columns.name: linked_registry_id
columns.description: FK to the word_registry row being linked to. NULL in 7 rows, which therefore have only the text linked_word and cannot be resolved by join — those 7 links are unresolvable as data.

columns.name: connection_type_id
columns.description: Which of the 11 wa_crosslink_type relationships this is. Heavily skewed: types 1 and 2 account for 109 of 158 links, and several registered types are barely used.

columns.name: connecting_term
columns.description: The transliterated Hebrew or Greek term that carries the connection, e.g. 'ne.phesh' (7), 'na.cham' (4). Free text, not a Strong's number or an FK, so it cannot be joined to the term tables; NULL in 6 rows.

columns.name: note
columns.description: The researcher's prose explanation of the connection, citing verses where relevant — e.g. that ba.ash (to stink) appears in both the abomination and shame word sets. Populated for all 158 rows and the actual value of this table.

wa_data_quality_flags.description: Engine-derived data-quality evidence raised against a term in a word-study file (19,866 rows) — automated observations such as thin verse coverage or a concrete/physical gloss. All rows resolve to just 7 flag types, and the table has no resolution or soft-delete column, so it is an append-only log with no lifecycle.
wa_data_quality_flags.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_data_quality_flags (
    id               INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    strong_id        TEXT,
    verse_id         INTEGER,
    flag_id          INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_quality_flag_types(id),
    description      TEXT,
    corrective_action TEXT,
    correction_date  TEXT,
    delete_flagged   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    last_changed     TEXT
)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key. The range starts at 8,696, so several thousand earlier flags were deleted outright rather than soft-deleted.

columns.name: flag_id
columns.description: FK to wa_quality_flag_types. Only 7 distinct types are actually used, dominated by ids 4 (7,781), 47 (5,759) and 3 (5,014); the flag's meaning lives in the type table, not here.

columns.name: description
columns.description: The flag's specific evidence text, e.g. 'sabaōth (hosts, occ=67) — 2 verses, 3% coverage' — the per-row detail that makes the flag actionable.

columns.name: last_changed
columns.description: Populated on only 323 of 19,866 rows and with just 4 distinct values from March 2026. The field was effectively abandoned; row age cannot be established from this table.

wa_dim_review_cluster_log.description: A completion log for the retired dimension review: one row per C-code cluster finished, six in all (C10, C13, C17, C20, C21, C22), recorded between 2026-04-09 and 2026-05-02. Against the 22 C-codes present in wa_dimension_index it shows the review was closed out for only six clusters before the layer was abandoned.
wa_dim_review_cluster_log.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_dim_review_cluster_log (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
  cluster TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
  completed_date TEXT NOT NULL,
  instruction_version TEXT NOT NULL,
  registry_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  group_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  anchored_count INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  notes TEXT,
  last_modified TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now'))
)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the log entry.

columns.name: cluster
columns.description: The C-code completed, unique per row — the natural key of the log.

columns.name: completed_date
columns.description: The date the cluster's review was signed off.

columns.name: instruction_version
columns.description: The exact instruction document the review was performed under. All six rows name a different version, spanning v1.7 to v3_3, which shows the method was still changing while the reviews were being run.

columns.name: registry_count
columns.description: How many word registries the cluster's review covered.

columns.name: group_count
columns.description: How many verse_context_groups were reviewed, from 46 to 370.

columns.name: anchored_count
columns.description: How many groups were anchored. Zero on five of the six rows and 114 on one, so the field was only actually populated for a single cluster.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: The reviewer's closing narrative for the cluster — which registries were covered, what was excluded and why, and any rewrites. The substance of the log.

wa_dimension_index.description: The retired dimension-review layer: 3,509 rows, one per verse_context_group, recording which of 20 named dimensions the group was assigned to and how its verses were triaged into anchor, related and set-aside. Written between 2026-04-06 and 2026-05-02 under the C-code cluster scheme and not touched since; superseded by the M-code cluster and finding model.
wa_dimension_index.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_dimension_index (
        id                    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
        verse_context_group_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES verse_context_group(id),
        owning_registry_no    INTEGER NOT NULL,
        cluster_assignment    TEXT,
        dimension             TEXT,
        anchor_count          INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        related_count         INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        set_aside_count       INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        total_verse_count     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
        delete_flagged        INTEGER DEFAULT 0
    , dimension_confidence TEXT DEFAULT NULL, manual_override INTEGER DEFAULT 0, notes TEXT DEFAULT NULL, last_modified TEXT DEFAULT NULL, dominant_subject TEXT DEFAULT NULL)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the index entry.

columns.name: verse_context_group_id
columns.description: The verse_context_group being classified. Unique across all 3,509 rows — the table is strictly one entry per group.

columns.name: owning_registry_no
columns.description: The word_registry the group belongs to. 173 distinct registries, unevenly loaded (registry 187 alone has 200 groups).

columns.name: cluster_assignment
columns.description: The C-code (C01 to C22) of the retired dimension-review scheme. Uncontrolled vocabulary and superseded by the M-code cluster model, though the data is retained.

columns.name: dimension
columns.description: The named dimension assigned, such as '05 — Moral Character' or '02 — Emotion — Negative'. 20 values, NULL on 244 rows — precisely the rows whose confidence is UNCLASSIFIED.

columns.name: anchor_count
columns.description: How many verses in the group were treated as anchors for the dimension. Almost always 1 or 2.

columns.name: related_count
columns.description: How many verses were classed as related rather than anchoring.

columns.name: set_aside_count
columns.description: How many verses were set aside as not bearing on the dimension — the review's rejection tally.

columns.name: total_verse_count
columns.description: The group's verse total. Intended to reconcile with the three counts above, but nothing in the schema enforces that.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker; set on 29 entries.

columns.name: dimension_confidence
columns.description: How the dimension was arrived at, and the field that shows the review's reliability: KEYWORD_WEAK (1,542) and KEYWORD_STRONG are automated keyword matches, CLAUDE_AI (1,286) a model reading, ROOT_INFERRED a root-family inference, UNCLASSIFIED (244) no assignment at all. Uncontrolled vocabulary; nearly half the entries rest on a weak keyword match.

columns.name: manual_override
columns.description: Marks the 190 entries where the researcher overrode the automated assignment.

columns.name: notes
columns.description: Free-prose justification for the assignment, present on about 40 per cent of entries; often records that an automated label was corrected and why.

profile.max: tufloō — god of this world blinding the minds of unbelievers (2Cor 4:4). AV grounds mind-blinding by adversarial agency;… (+126 chars)

columns.name: last_modified
columns.description: When the entry was last written. Confined to April and early May 2026 and recorded in three inconsistent formats (bare date, ISO without zone, ISO with Z).

columns.name: dominant_subject
columns.description: Who the group's verses are principally about: HUMAN (969), GOD, NONE, OTHER_HUMAN, UNSEEN. NULL on 2,321 rows, so it was only ever filled in for a minority. Uncontrolled vocabulary.

wa_file_index.description: One row per input file (or engine onboarding stub) that supplied a registry word's data, with the file's provenance, split-part structure and specification version. CLAUDE.md marks it legacy — joins should use the bypass FK word_registry_fk rather than routing through this table — and its metadata columns are inconsistently filled across the eras it spans.
wa_file_index.sql:
CREATE TABLE "wa_file_index" (
    id                           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    filename                     TEXT NOT NULL,
    registry_id                  TEXT NOT NULL,
    word_registry_fk             INTEGER REFERENCES word_registry(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
    word                         TEXT NOT NULL,
    part_number                  INTEGER,
    total_parts                  INTEGER,
    is_split                     INTEGER,
    schema_version               TEXT,
    phase                        TEXT,
    produced_date                TEXT,
    source_file                  TEXT,
    translation_used             TEXT,
    specification                TEXT,
    revision_note                TEXT,
    source_list                  TEXT,
    category                     TEXT,
    testament_coverage           TEXT,
    root_families_in_prior_parts TEXT,
    last_changed                 TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now'))
)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the file entry. Runs to 344 across 308 rows, so some entries have been removed.

columns.name: filename
columns.description: DEFECT: the column names a file but 148 of 308 rows hold an engine run id instead ('RUN-20260318_134133-BULK_GAP_FILL', 132 rows alone), not a filename. Only the remaining rows carry real names such as '01-wa-117-peace-data-part1-20260317-v1.json', so the column mixes two different kinds of identifier.

columns.name: registry_id
columns.description: The registry word the file supplied, as TEXT. 195 distinct values, and unlike word_run_state.registry_id none is zero-padded here — the two tables format the same identifier differently.

columns.name: word_registry_fk
columns.description: The integer FK to word_registry.id, with ON DELETE RESTRICT. This is the authoritative join per programme rule; prefer it over registry_id, which is TEXT and inconsistently formatted across tables.

columns.name: word
columns.description: The English registry word the file relates to, a convenience copy. Notable that 5 rows carry 'read-surfaced characteristics', which is not a registry word — evidence of a non-registry entry being filed here.

columns.name: part_number
columns.description: Which part this file is where a word's data was split across files, 1-3. NULL in 269 of 308 rows because most words are single-file.

columns.name: total_parts
columns.description: How many parts the word's data was split into, 1-3. NULL in the same 269 rows as part_number, and the counts are internally inconsistent — 24 rows claim total_parts=3 but only 8 rows carry part_number=3.

columns.name: is_split
columns.description: Whether the word's data was split across files: 0 in 171 rows, 1 in 36, NULL in 101. The 101 NULLs mean the flag cannot be trusted as a complete answer without consulting part_number.

columns.name: schema_version
columns.description: The schema version in force when the file was produced, e.g. '3.37.0' (71), '2.3' (40), '3.40.0' (26). Spans two incompatible numbering eras (2.x and 3.x) and is NULL in 150 rows.

columns.name: phase
columns.description: Which pipeline phase produced the file. Nominally always Phase 1, but recorded twelve different ways — 'Phase 1', 'Phase 1 (audit_word add-terms)', and three variants of the STEP assimilation label differing only in their dash character ('—', '---', '-'). A clear case of uncontrolled free text.

columns.name: produced_date
columns.description: The date the file was produced, ISO date only. 141 of 308 rows share 2026-03-18, the date of the bulk gap-fill.

columns.name: source_file
columns.description: The upstream document the data was taken from, e.g. 'word_fear.md', '200_energy_step_data_20260328.json'. NULL in 251 of 308 rows, so upstream provenance is recorded for only a fifth of entries.

columns.name: translation_used
columns.description: Which Bible translation the file's verse text came from. Only ever 'ESV' (206 rows), NULL in the other 102 — it records a constant, not a variable.

columns.name: specification
columns.description: Which Session A instruction version governed the file's production, e.g. 'Session A v9 Automation' (151), 'Session A Instruction v7'. Free text and NULL in 101 rows.

columns.name: revision_note
columns.description: Free-text note about how or why the entry was revised, e.g. that a stub was auto-created by audit_word onboarding, or that a word's file was orphaned by a registry merge. Present in 108 rows and the only record of several one-off data decisions.

columns.name: last_changed
columns.description: When the entry was last written, defaulting to datetime('now'). DEFECT of format: values here are space-separated ('2026-03-16 11:32:38') rather than the ISO-8601 T-separated form used across the rest of the schema, because the default calls datetime() rather than strftime().

wa_file_name_pattern.description: The 23 registered filename conventions used across the programme, each given as a template such as 'wa-dim-{cluster}-extract-{YYYYMMDD}.json' with the instruction that governs it. It is documentation held as data — nothing enforces these patterns, and the table has been unchanged since its single 2026-04-20 load.
wa_file_name_pattern.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_file_name_pattern (
            id                        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            pattern_code              TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
            pattern                   TEXT    NOT NULL,
            scope                     TEXT,
            description               TEXT,
            governing_instruction     TEXT,
            deprecated                INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            deprecation_note          TEXT,
            created_at                TEXT    NOT NULL,
            last_modified             TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the pattern, 1-23.

columns.name: pattern_code
columns.description: Short handle for the pattern, e.g. 'dim_cluster_extract', 'dim_grpdesc_patch'. Unique per row.

columns.name: pattern
columns.description: The filename template itself, with braced placeholders, e.g. 'wa-dim-{cluster}-grpverify-{group_code}-{YYYYMMDD}.json'. Placeholder names are conventional and not defined anywhere.

columns.name: scope
columns.description: What the pattern is instantiated per: 'per-cluster' 8, 'per-registry' 8, 'programme' 3, plus per-group, per-batch and patch-id. Uncontrolled by CHECK.

columns.name: description
columns.description: What kind of artefact the pattern names, e.g. 'DimReview per-registry patch'. Populated for all 23.

columns.name: governing_instruction
columns.description: Which document defines the convention, e.g. 'wa-dimensionreview-instruction [current] §15' (11 rows). Reveals that half the registered patterns belong to the retired dimension-review layer.

columns.name: deprecated
columns.description: Whether the pattern is retired. 0 in all 23 rows — no pattern has been retired, including the dimension-review ones whose layer is no longer live.

columns.name: deprecation_note
columns.description: Intended to explain a retirement, but NULL in all 23 rows.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When the pattern was registered. Identical ('2026-04-20T15:55:54') across all 23 rows — one bulk load.

columns.name: last_modified
columns.description: When the pattern was last changed. NULL in all 23 rows: no registered pattern has ever been amended since the load.

wa_finding_catalogue_links.description: The legacy mapping of Session B findings to catalogue questions, with a coverage judgement and a note on what the finding contributed. It is the predecessor of finding_question_link, points at wa_session_b_findings rather than the live finding table, and was written in April and May 2026; unlike its successor it exercises 375 of the catalogue's questions and records real coverage verdicts.
wa_finding_catalogue_links.sql:
CREATE TABLE "wa_finding_catalogue_links" (
        id              INTEGER  PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
        finding_id      INTEGER  REFERENCES wa_session_b_findings(id),
        question_id     INTEGER  NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_obs_question_catalogue(obs_id),
        coverage        TEXT,
        status          TEXT     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'suggested',
        pattern_type    TEXT,
        mapped_date     TEXT,
        validated_date  TEXT,
        validated_by    TEXT,
        session_b_note  TEXT,
        delete_flagged  INTEGER  NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
        UNIQUE (finding_id, question_id)
    )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key, also referenced by wa_prose_section_citations.cited_qa_link_id.

columns.name: finding_id
columns.description: The Session B finding being mapped, referencing wa_session_b_findings. Null on 743 rows — these are the 'no_finding'/'not_applicable' rows that record a question was considered but nothing answered it, which is itself the evidence.

columns.name: question_id
columns.description: The catalogue question, referencing wa_obs_question_catalogue.obs_id. 375 distinct questions are covered, far more than the 31 the live finding_question_link reaches.

columns.name: coverage
columns.description: How well the finding answers the question: full, partial, not_applicable or no_finding. The negative verdicts are deliberate records of a gap, not missing data.

columns.name: status
columns.description: Whether the mapping is merely active or has been validated. The column defaults to 'suggested' but no row holds that value, so the default is dead.

columns.name: pattern_type
columns.description: Free-text characterisation of what the mapping represents (for example 'synthesis_source (D)', 'New finding', 'Gap identified'). Badly uncontrolled — it holds empty strings, and the same idea appears both plain and markdown-italicised ('New finding' and '*New finding*').

columns.name: mapped_date
columns.description: When the finding was mapped to the question; 18 distinct timestamps show batch authoring rather than incremental work.

columns.name: validated_date
columns.description: When the mapping was validated. It equals mapped_date on 6,055 of 6,199 rows, so for almost every row validation carries no independent timing information.

columns.name: validated_by
columns.description: Which analytical pass validated the mapping — a first-tier or second-tier Claude AI run. Null on the 488 rows marked 'validated', which is the inverse of what the name implies.

columns.name: session_b_note
columns.description: Prose explaining what the finding contributes to the question — the substantive commentary of the mapping. Some rows hold an empty string rather than a note.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker; 414 mappings are flagged out.

wa_finding_entity_links.description: A legacy link from Session B findings to the verses or verse-context groups they attach to, superseded by finding_verse_link under the live model. Small and closed: 287 rows written across three batch runs in late April 2026, covering only 49 findings, and nothing has been added or deleted since.
wa_finding_entity_links.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_finding_entity_links (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    finding_id      INTEGER NOT NULL,
    entity_type     TEXT NOT NULL,
    entity_id       INTEGER,
    entity_strongs  TEXT,
    raised_date     TEXT NOT NULL, delete_flagged INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    FOREIGN KEY (finding_id) REFERENCES wa_session_b_findings(id)
)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key for the link row.

columns.name: finding_id
columns.description: The Session B finding, referencing wa_session_b_findings. Only 49 distinct findings appear, each linked to up to fourteen entities.

columns.name: entity_type
columns.description: What the finding is linked to — 'verse' or 'group'. Uncontrolled, and it determines which table entity_id should be read against.

columns.name: entity_id
columns.description: The id of the linked verse record or verse-context group, its meaning depending on entity_type. Polymorphic, so no FK can enforce it and integrity rests on convention.

columns.name: entity_strongs
columns.description: Intended to record the Strong's number of the linked entity, but 100% NULL — declared and never populated in any of the 287 rows.

columns.name: raised_date
columns.description: When the link was made. Only three distinct timestamps, confirming three batch runs produced the entire table.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker; never used — all rows remain live.

wa_flag_type_question_link.description: Maps quality-flag types to the catalogue questions that a raised flag should prompt, so that a data-quality signal pulls in the right analytical prompts. Tiny and static: twelve rows, all written in one run on 20 April 2026, all connecting four flag types to the Q-COV coverage question family.
wa_flag_type_question_link.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_flag_type_question_link (
            id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            flag_type_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_quality_flag_types(id),
            question_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_obs_question_catalogue(obs_id),
            context_note    TEXT,
            active          INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
            created_at      TEXT,
            UNIQUE (flag_type_id, question_id)
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key for the link row.

columns.name: flag_type_id
columns.description: The quality flag type, referencing wa_quality_flag_types. Only four types participate, each triggering two to four questions.

columns.name: question_id
columns.description: The catalogue question the flag prompts, referencing wa_obs_question_catalogue.obs_id. Each question appears exactly once, so no question is triggered by more than one flag type.

columns.name: context_note
columns.description: A human-readable label naming the question the link points at (for example 'Q-COV-01 — alternative-term coverage'). It duplicates catalogue content rather than adding context specific to the flag.

columns.name: active
columns.description: Whether the link is in force. Every row is 1, so the column has never distinguished anything.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: Insertion timestamp. A single value across all twelve rows — the whole table was seeded at once.

wa_label_pattern.description: The 11 registered identifier formats used for labels rather than filenames — finding ids, flag ids, patch ids, group codes — each mapped to the column it populates. Like wa_file_name_pattern it is documentation-as-data with no enforcement, untouched since its 2026-04-20 load.
wa_label_pattern.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_label_pattern (
            id                        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            pattern_code              TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
            pattern                   TEXT    NOT NULL,
            entity                    TEXT,
            description               TEXT,
            governing_instruction     TEXT,
            deprecated                INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            deprecation_note          TEXT,
            created_at                TEXT    NOT NULL,
            last_modified             TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the pattern, 1-11.

columns.name: pattern_code
columns.description: Short handle for the identifier format, e.g. 'dim_finding', 'patch_id', 'group_code'. Unique per row.

columns.name: pattern
columns.description: The identifier template, e.g. 'DIM-{registry_no}-{3-digit-sequence}', 'PATCH-{YYYYMMDD}-{NNN}-{TYPE}-V{n}'. Note 'PATCH-{YYYYMMDD}-{NNN}-{TYPE}-V{n}' is registered in wa_file_name_pattern too, so the same template is recorded in two tables.

columns.name: entity
columns.description: Which column the identifier populates, e.g. 'wa_session_research_flags.flag_label', 'verse_context_group.group_code'. Given as a dotted string, so it is readable but not a checkable reference.

columns.name: description
columns.description: What the identifier denotes, usually with an example, e.g. 'Dimension Review Session B finding — e.g. DIM-112-004'. Two rows share the description 'Pre-DIM prefix format (legacy; reconciliation pending)'.

columns.name: deprecated
columns.description: Whether the format is retired. 0 in all 11 rows, despite one being described in its own text as legacy with reconciliation pending.

columns.name: deprecation_note

columns.name: created_at

wa_lsj_parsed.description: Structured parse of the Liddell-Scott-Jones classical Greek lexicon entry for a term, splitting the raw entry into gloss, domains, and philosophical and etymological notes. wa_meaning_parsed.description: One header row per inventory term for its parsed definition, holding the counts and derived flags of the parse whose detail lives in wa_meaning_sense and wa_meaning_stem. 7,748 rows, one-to-one with the term (term_inv_id is unique). Note the language column is broken: it reads 'Hebrew' for 2,386 rows whose term is actually Greek or Aramaic.
wa_meaning_parsed.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_meaning_parsed (
            id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            term_inv_id         INTEGER NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES wa_term_inventory(id),
            strongs_number      TEXT    NOT NULL,
            language            TEXT    NOT NULL,
            top_sense_count     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            stem_count          INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            has_causative_stem  INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            has_domain_tags     INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            parsed_at           TEXT    NOT NULL,
            parse_version       TEXT    NOT NULL,
            parse_warnings      TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the parse record; referenced as parsed_meaning_id by wa_meaning_sense and wa_meaning_stem, and mirrored back onto wa_term_inventory.parsed_meaning_id.

columns.name: term_inv_id
columns.description: The inventory term whose meaning was parsed, pointing to wa_term_inventory.id. Unique across the table — exactly one parse per term.

columns.name: strongs_number
columns.description: Declared NOT NULL but functionally empty: 7,736 of 7,748 rows hold an empty string, and only 12 carry a real Strong's. The term's Strong's must be read from wa_term_inventory instead.

columns.name: language
columns.description: Nominally the language of the parsed term, and demonstrably wrong. Only the 9 rows with a real Strong's are correctly marked Greek; 'Hebrew' is written by default on everything else, so 2,199 Greek terms and 187 Aramaic terms are mislabelled Hebrew — 31 per cent of the table. Do not use this column; join to wa_term_inventory.language.

columns.name: top_sense_count
columns.description: How many top-level senses the parse found in the definition text. 7,499 of 7,748 terms have exactly one; the maximum observed is 6, and 9 rows have zero.

columns.name: stem_count
columns.description: How many Hebrew verbal stems the parse broke out. Zero on 7,745 of 7,748 rows — only three terms ever received a stem breakdown, which matches the 13 rows in wa_meaning_stem.

columns.name: has_causative_stem
columns.description: 1 where the parsed definition evidences a causative stem (the term causes the inner state in another); set on 973 terms. Populated far more widely than stem_count, so it is detected from the definition text directly rather than from the stem breakdown.

columns.name: has_domain_tags
columns.description: Declared to mark parses carrying semantic domain tags, but 0 on every one of the 7,748 rows — domain tagging was designed and never performed, consistent with wa_meaning_sense.domain_tag being wholly NULL.

columns.name: parsed_at
columns.description: When the definition was parsed, ranging March to July 2026 across 309 distinct timestamps — unlike most tables in this group, the parse has been run incrementally as terms were added.

columns.name: parse_version
columns.description: Version of the parser that produced the row; uniformly '1.0.0', so every parse in the table came from one unrevised implementation.

columns.name: parse_warnings
columns.description: JSON array of issues the parser hit. Only one warning has ever been emitted — 'PROSE_ONLY', on 5,652 rows, meaning the definition had no numbered structure to parse. That is 73 per cent of the table, so for most terms the sense hierarchy below is a single prose blob rather than a real parse.

wa_meaning_sense.description: The parsed sense hierarchy of a term's definition: 17,125 rows, one per numbered sense, keyed to wa_meaning_parsed and ordered by the source's own numbering (1, 1a, 1a1 and so on). Three of its columns — stem_label, domain_tag and is_homonym — were designed to enrich the hierarchy and carry no data at all, so the table delivers plain nesting only.
wa_meaning_sense.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_meaning_sense (
            id                 INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            parsed_meaning_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_meaning_parsed(id),
            level_code         TEXT    NOT NULL,
            level_depth        INTEGER NOT NULL,
            parent_level_code  TEXT,
            sense_text         TEXT,
            is_stem_label      INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            stem_label         TEXT,
            domain_tag         TEXT,
            sort_order         INTEGER NOT NULL
        , is_homonym INTEGER DEFAULT 0)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the sense row.

columns.name: parsed_meaning_id
columns.description: The parse this sense belongs to, pointing to wa_meaning_parsed.id. 7,745 distinct parses, averaging just over two senses each.

columns.name: level_code
columns.description: The sense's own label from the source definition — '1' for a top-level sense, '1a' for its first subsense, '1a1' below that. This is the human-readable position in the hierarchy, and every parse has a '1' (7,739 rows).

columns.name: level_depth
columns.description: How deep the sense sits: 1 (8,050 rows), 2 (8,719) or 3 (356). Nesting never exceeds three levels in the current data.

columns.name: parent_level_code
columns.description: The level_code of the sense's parent, populated only for third-level senses (356 rows) — top and second-level senses leave it NULL rather than pointing upward, so the parent chain is reconstructed from level_code, not this column.

columns.name: sense_text
columns.description: The definition text of this sense — the substantive content of the row. 7,664 distinct values over 17,125 rows because many senses are short and common phrasings recur.

profile.max: § to send to hell, hold captive in Tartarus; a derivative of the Greek noun "Tartarus," a place of torture and torment l… (+258 chars)

columns.name: is_stem_label
columns.description: Declared to mark a sense row that is really a Hebrew stem heading rather than a sense, but 0 on all 17,125 rows — never used.

columns.name: stem_label
columns.description: Declared to name the stem for a stem-heading row, but NULL on all 17,125 rows — never populated.

columns.name: domain_tag
columns.description: Declared to carry the sense's semantic domain, but NULL on all 17,125 rows — never populated, matching has_domain_tags being 0 throughout wa_meaning_parsed.

columns.name: sort_order
columns.description: Display position of the sense within its parse; 0 marks the first (7,745 rows, one per parse) and it rises to 34 for the most heavily subdivided definitions.

columns.name: is_homonym
columns.description: Declared to mark senses belonging to a distinct homonym of the lemma, but 0 on all 17,125 rows — homonym separation was never carried out.

wa_meaning_stem.description: Breaks a Hebrew verb's definition down by verbal stem (Qal, Piel, Hiphil and so on) with the sense each stem carries. Effectively unused: 13 rows covering just 3 terms, against 7,748 parses — the stem layer was built and then abandoned, as wa_meaning_parsed.stem_count being 0 on 7,745 rows confirms.
wa_meaning_stem.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_meaning_stem (
            id                INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            parsed_meaning_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_meaning_parsed(id),
            stem_name         TEXT    NOT NULL,
            stem_type         TEXT,
            sense_count       INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
            top_sense_text    TEXT
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the stem row.

columns.name: parsed_meaning_id
columns.description: The parse the stem belongs to, pointing to wa_meaning_parsed.id. Only three parses are represented, with 6, 5 and 2 stems respectively.

columns.name: stem_name
columns.description: The Hebrew verbal stem named in the definition — Qal, Niphal, Piel, Hiphil, Hithpael and Hithpolel appear among the 13 rows.

columns.name: stem_type
columns.description: What the stem does to the verb's sense: 'base' (5), 'intensive' (4), 'causative' (3) and one 'piel_causative'. The last value straddles the naming scheme, mixing a stem name into what is otherwise a type vocabulary.

columns.name: sense_count
columns.description: How many senses the definition gives under this stem, from 0 to 9; four of the 13 rows have none.

columns.name: top_sense_text
columns.description: The leading sense the term carries in this stem (e.g. 'to be set apart, be consecrated'), which is the point of the breakdown — how the stem shifts the meaning. Distinct on all 13 rows.

wa_obs_question_catalogue.description: The observation question catalogue: 424 prompts that drive analysis, organised by tier and component, each with its text, scope, provenance and lifecycle status. Its state is the notable thing — 243 of 424 rows are marked deleted and only 239 are 'active', the residue of a v2 restructure that retired 159 questions as redundant; note also that deleted and status disagree in count, so the two lifecycle markers are not kept consistent.
wa_obs_question_catalogue.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_obs_question_catalogue (
    obs_id            INTEGER  PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    question_code     TEXT     NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    section           TEXT     NOT NULL,
    source_word       TEXT,
    source_registry_no INTEGER  REFERENCES word_registry(id),
    question_text     TEXT     NOT NULL,
    pattern_type      TEXT,
    scope             TEXT     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'universal',
    status            TEXT     NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
    deleted           INTEGER  NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    date_added        TEXT     NOT NULL,
    catalogue_version TEXT     NOT NULL
, review_note TEXT, tier TEXT, component_code TEXT, component_title TEXT, prompt_seq INTEGER)

columns.name: obs_id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key for the question, referenced by finding_question_link.question_id and wa_finding_catalogue_links.question_id.

columns.name: question_code
columns.description: The stable human-facing identifier for the question (for example 'C-001', 'WS-006'). Unique across the catalogue; the varied prefixes record the different families the catalogue accreted from.

columns.name: section
columns.description: The report section or tier the question belongs under, in long descriptive form (for example 'Section 3 — Annotated Verse Evidence', 'T3 — The Inner Faculties'). Free text with 27 variants and two competing naming schemes — 'Section N' and 'Tn' — running side by side.

columns.name: source_registry_no
columns.description: The word_registry id matching source_word, where the question came from a specific word study. Null on half the rows, which are programme-level.

columns.name: question_text
columns.description: The question itself as it is put to the analysis — the substantive content of the catalogue. Unique per row.

wa_patch_type_registry.description: The 20 recognised JSON patch types, each naming the instruction that governs it and the tables it writes to — the reference-as-database record of what a patch of a given type is allowed to do. wa_prose_section_citations.description: Records which evidence a given prose section cites — a finding, a Q&A catalogue link, an SD pointer, or an observation sequence — together with the citation marker as it appears in the text. It covers only 25 prose sections out of 1,039 and was written in five batches in late April 2026; all its FKs point at the legacy Session B evidence tables, so it documents the old citation model rather than the live finding store.
wa_prose_section_citations.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_prose_section_citations (
            id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            prose_section_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES prose_section(id),
            cited_finding_id    INTEGER REFERENCES wa_session_b_findings(id),
            cited_qa_link_id    INTEGER REFERENCES wa_finding_catalogue_links(id),
            cited_sd_pointer_id INTEGER REFERENCES wa_session_research_flags(id),
            cited_observation_seq TEXT,                -- e.g. 'OBS-026' as raw token from prose
            citation_form       TEXT NOT NULL,         -- the literal text in the prose
            paragraph_no        INTEGER,               -- optional: which paragraph in the section
            delete_flagged      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            created_at          TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))
        )

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key for the citation row.

columns.name: prose_section_id
columns.description: The prose section doing the citing. Only 25 distinct sections appear, so citation tracking was piloted on a small set and never rolled out.

columns.name: cited_finding_id
columns.description: The cited finding, referencing the legacy wa_session_b_findings table rather than the live finding store. Null on 45% of rows, which cite something other than a finding.

columns.name: cited_qa_link_id
columns.description: The cited wa_finding_catalogue_links row (a finding-to-question mapping). Present on only four rows — effectively unused.

columns.name: cited_sd_pointer_id
columns.description: The cited Session D research pointer in wa_session_research_flags. Present on 38 rows.

columns.name: cited_observation_seq
columns.description: The cited observation as a textual sequence code (for example 'OBS-067-OBS-014'), used where the observation has no row to point at.

columns.name: citation_form
columns.description: The citation marker exactly as it appears in the prose — 'Q001', 'DIM-067-SD002', 'SP-067-018' and similar. This is the only column populated on every row, and the several distinct prefix families show the citation notation was never standardised.

columns.name: paragraph_no
columns.description: The paragraph of the prose section in which the citation occurs. 96% NULL, so the position of a citation within its section was almost never recorded.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: Soft-delete marker; no row has been flagged.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: Insertion timestamp. Only five distinct values, confirming the table is the output of five batch runs on 27 and 28 April 2026.

wa_quality_flag_types.description: Lookup of the 29 data-quality and research flag codes, grouped by kind and each defined in prose. Unlike phase2_flag_types it carries a deprecation mechanism and has been through at least one merge (THIN_DATA folded into VERSE_EVIDENCE_CONCENTRATED), so 4 codes are retired but retained.
wa_quality_flag_types.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_quality_flag_types (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    flag_group    TEXT NOT NULL,
    flag_code     TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    description   TEXT,
    delete_flagged INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    deprecation_note TEXT,
    category      TEXT,
    research_actions TEXT
)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the flag type. The values are not contiguous (1-4 then 23-24 among the top), so codes have been deleted from the lookup over time.

columns.name: flag_group
columns.description: The flag's family: DATA_COVERAGE 9, DATA_QUALITY 6, RESEARCHER_DECISION 3, SESSION_B 3, SESSION_D_POINTER 3, and two smaller groups. Uncontrolled by CHECK.

columns.name: flag_code
columns.description: The flag's code, e.g. 'CANDIDATE_REGISTRY_WORD', 'DATA_INTEGRITY', 'PH2_BOUNDARY_QUESTION'. Unique, and the value stored when a flag is raised against a record.

columns.name: description
columns.description: The prose criterion for the flag — when it applies and what it obliges. Populated for all 29 rows.

columns.name: deprecation_note
columns.description: Why the code was retired and where its meaning went, e.g. 'Merged into VERSE_EVIDENCE_CONCENTRATED (id=3) in M29 (2026-04-20). All existing THIN_DATA rows repointed'. Present for the 4 deprecated codes.

columns.name: category
columns.description: A second grouping axis that largely duplicates flag_group — its four values (DATA_QUALITY, RESEARCHER_DECISION, SESSION_D_POINTER, STUDY_REQUIRED) all appear in flag_group with the same counts. NULL in 14 rows, so it is a partly-populated redundant column.

columns.name: research_actions
columns.description: Semicolon-separated codes for the follow-up actions a flag triggers, e.g. 'R_STEP_EXHAUST_CHECK;R_AI_WIDER_CONTEXT'. Present for only 4 rows, and the action codes themselves are not defined in any lookup table.

wa_rule_registry.description: The programme's global rules held as data: 59 rules with their text, rationale, application notes and supersession chain, all imported from a single JSON document. wa_session_b_findings.description: The superseded per-word Session B findings store: 2,883 findings raised April to May 2026 across 112 registries, since replaced by the universal finding table. wa_session_research_flags.description: Researcher-facing pointers and findings raised during analysis (715 rows) — a working queue of things to return to, with routing (session_target, cluster_link) and a resolution lifecycle. It has genuine vocabulary drift: priority holds both 'MEDIUM'/'HIGH'/'LOW' and lower-case 'normal'/'advisory', and session_target holds both 'D' and 'Session D', 'B' and 'Session B', 'Researcher' and 'researcher' — the same value spelled several ways with no CHECK to stop it.
wa_session_research_flags.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_session_research_flags (
            id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
            registry_id         INTEGER NOT NULL,
            file_id             INTEGER,
            flag_code           TEXT    NOT NULL,
            flag_label          TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,
            strongs_reference   TEXT,
            cross_registry_id   INTEGER,
            priority            TEXT    DEFAULT 'MEDIUM',
            session_target      TEXT    DEFAULT 'D',
            description         TEXT    NOT NULL,
            session_raised      TEXT    NOT NULL,
            raised_date         TEXT    NOT NULL,
            resolved            INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            resolved_date       TEXT,
            resolved_note       TEXT, cluster_link TEXT, cluster_link_basis TEXT,
            FOREIGN KEY (registry_id) REFERENCES word_registry(id),
            FOREIGN KEY (file_id) REFERENCES wa_file_index(id),
            FOREIGN KEY (cross_registry_id) REFERENCES word_registry(id)
        )

wa_term_inventory.description: The per-registry term inventory: one row per term as held under a given English word's file, carrying the STEP-sourced identity, gloss, meaning text, occurrence count, testament span and — critically — term_owner_type, which marks whether this is the term's canonical home (OWNER) or a cross-reference copy (XREF). At 7,844 rows it parallels mti_terms closely, but it is the registry-facing view: the same Strong's recurs across registries, giving 4,155 distinct Strong's over 7,844 rows.
wa_term_inventory.sql:
CREATE TABLE "wa_term_inventory" (
    id                          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    file_id                     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_file_index(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
    language                    TEXT NOT NULL,
    term_id                     TEXT NOT NULL,
    strongs_number              TEXT,
    transliteration             TEXT NOT NULL,
    step_search_gloss           TEXT,
    word_analysis_gloss         TEXT,
    occurrence_count            INTEGER,
    occurrence_count_qualifier  TEXT,
    meaning                     TEXT,
    meaning_numbered            TEXT,
    also_spelled                TEXT,
    lsj_entry                   TEXT,
    testament                   TEXT,
    causative_form_present      INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    last_changed                TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    short_def_mounce            TEXT,
    parsed_meaning_id           INTEGER
, delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0, evidential_status TEXT DEFAULT NULL, retention_note TEXT DEFAULT NULL, term_owner_type TEXT DEFAULT NULL, term_introduction_source TEXT, term_introduction_rationale TEXT, term_introduction_date TEXT, word_registry_fk INTEGER)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the term-in-registry record; referenced as term_inv_id by the related-words, root-family, flag and meaning-parse tables.

columns.name: file_id
columns.description: Foreign key to wa_file_index.id, the legacy per-registry file record this term was ingested under. wa_file_index is legacy and should not be joined through — use word_registry_fk on this table instead.

columns.name: language
columns.description: Source language of the term: Hebrew (5,423), Greek (2,231), Aramaic (190). Uncontrolled vocabulary, but unlike lexicon it does classify Aramaic properly.

columns.name: term_id
columns.description: The term's working identifier, normally the Strong's number. Not uniformly so: 17 rows use a descriptive fallback such as 'alupos_G_unconfirmed' where no Strong's was settled, so the column is a term key rather than a strict Strong's field.

columns.name: strongs_number
columns.description: The term's Strong's number, H/G plus four zero-padded digits. Null on 9 rows, and some rows carry a placeholder such as 'NO STRONG-135-metameleia' instead of a real number.

columns.name: transliteration
columns.description: Romanised lemma, declared NOT NULL but with rows holding only whitespace; never to be cited without the gloss.

columns.name: step_search_gloss
columns.description: The gloss as returned by STEP when the term was found — the source-of-record English sense, preserved unedited.

columns.name: word_analysis_gloss
columns.description: The gloss as it appears in STEP's word-analysis view. Nearly identical in cardinality to step_search_gloss (2,871 vs 2,873 distinct), so the two rarely disagree; holding both records that STEP exposes the gloss in two places.

columns.name: occurrence_count
columns.description: Corpus occurrence count for the term per STEP, up to 10,284. Null on 20 rows, and 0 is a real value for terms with no attested occurrence.

columns.name: occurrence_count_qualifier
columns.description: Caveat on the occurrence count where it is not exact — chiefly 'about' (636 rows) for an approximate figure. The remaining values ('image', 'to transform', a note on an Aramaic equivalent) are not qualifiers at all but stray content in the wrong column.

wa_term_phase2_flags.description: Junction attaching Phase 2 triage flags from phase2_flag_types to inventory terms: 1,570 assignments over 883 terms, using 25 distinct flag types.         )

wa_term_related_words.description: The related-word web: 103,944 rows attaching each inventory term to other lemmas STEP reports as related, by gloss, transliteration and Strong's. Overwhelmingly a bulk import of STEP's relatedNos field with no editorial layer — of a 34,641-row sample only 105 rows carry any relationship note at all, and none is soft-deleted.
wa_term_related_words.sql:
CREATE TABLE "wa_term_related_words" (
    id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    term_inv_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_term_inventory(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    gloss               TEXT,
    transliteration     TEXT,
    strongs_number      TEXT,
    relationship_note   TEXT
, delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the related-word row.

columns.name: term_inv_id
columns.description: The inventory term the relation hangs off, pointing to wa_term_inventory.id and cascading on its deletion. Around 7,151 distinct terms appear in the sample, i.e. nearly the whole inventory carries related words, averaging well over a dozen apiece.

columns.name: gloss
columns.description: English sense of the related lemma — the readable identifier for the relation, since the related word is not itself an inventory row.

columns.name: transliteration
columns.description: Romanised form of the related lemma; read alongside the gloss, never alone.

columns.name: strongs_number
columns.description: Strong's number of the related lemma, H/G plus four zero-padded digits. Null on a small fraction (528 of 34,641 sampled), where STEP named a related word without resolving it to a Strong's.

columns.name: relationship_note
columns.description: Free-text account of how the two lemmas relate. Almost never used — in the sample only 105 of 34,641 rows carry one, and 103 of those are the provenance stamp 'STEP relatedNos' rather than a substantive relation; only a couple are hand-written etymological notes.

wa_term_root_family.description: Assigns inventory terms to a shared etymological root family by root code, so terms from one root (e.g. CHARAH, 'burn/anger') can be worked together. 2,861 rows over 2,860 distinct terms — roughly a third of the inventory — grouped into 964 root codes, and mostly backfilled in April 2026 by clustering wa_term_related_words rather than by direct etymological research.
wa_term_root_family.sql:
CREATE TABLE "wa_term_root_family" (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    term_inv_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_term_inventory(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    root_code       TEXT NOT NULL,
    root_language   TEXT,
    root_gloss      TEXT,
    note            TEXT
, delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate key for the root-family membership row.

columns.name: term_inv_id
columns.description: The inventory term being assigned to a root, pointing to wa_term_inventory.id and cascading on its deletion. 2,860 distinct terms over 2,861 rows, so a term belongs to one root family and effectively never two.

columns.name: root_code
columns.description: The root family's identifier — the grouping key. Coding is not consistent: some codes are bare romanised roots (CHARAH), some are language-prefixed (HEB-tov), and one is the single character 'Ō'. 964 codes over 2,861 rows means many families have only one or two members.

columns.name: root_language
columns.description: Language of the root: Hebrew (1,442), Greek (784), one Aramaic. Null on 634 rows, which are therefore assigned to a root with no language recorded.

columns.name: root_gloss
columns.description: English sense of the root itself (e.g. 'burn/anger' for CHARAH), giving the meaning the family shares. Null on the same 634 rows as root_language, and some rows hold an empty string.

columns.name: note
columns.description: Provenance for the assignment. 2,188 of the 2,234 populated rows are the same stamp — backfilled 2026-04-09 from wa_term_related_words clustering — so the great majority of this table is derived from STEP's related-word data, not from etymological judgement. The handful of remaining notes record genuine manual corrections, including a root-code collision between Hebrew charah and Greek charis.
