wa_verse_records.description: The legacy per-term-in-verse occurrence store (247,046 rows) that predates the master verse table — one row per term found in a verse, with the verse text, context, morphology and cluster/analysis markers denormalised onto it. It remains the anchor for verse_context, but it is heavily encumbered: 171,156 rows (69%) are soft-deleted, verse_id is NULL on some rows (the cause of the verse_evidence_orphan entries), and it duplicates verse_text and morph_code held authoritatively elsewhere.
wa_verse_records.sql:
CREATE TABLE "wa_verse_records" (
    id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    file_id             INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_file_index(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
    term_inv_id         INTEGER REFERENCES wa_term_inventory(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
    term_id             TEXT,
    transliteration     TEXT,
    testament           TEXT,
    reference           TEXT,
    verse_text          TEXT,
    last_changed        TEXT DEFAULT (datetime('now')),
    book_id             INTEGER REFERENCES books(id),
    chapter             INTEGER,
    verse_num           INTEGER,
    translation         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ESV',
    note                TEXT,
    claude_output       TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    target_word         TEXT,
    span_strong_match   INTEGER,
    context_before      TEXT,
    context_after       TEXT
, delete_flagged INTEGER DEFAULT 0, mti_term_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL, morph_code TEXT, stem TEXT, word_registry_fk INTEGER, verse_id INTEGER REFERENCES verse(id), analysis_marker TEXT, incorporated_in TEXT, verse_span_id INTEGER)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key for the term-in-verse occurrence; the target of verse_context.verse_record_id and wa_verse_term_links.verse_id.

columns.name: file_id
columns.description: FK to the legacy wa_file_index. Per project rule this is legacy scaffolding — joins should route via the bypass FKs (word_registry_fk, mti_term_id) rather than through file_index.

columns.name: term_inv_id
columns.description: FK to wa_term_inventory — the per-registry term entry (OWNER or XREF copy) this occurrence belongs to.

columns.name: term_id
columns.description: The term's identifier as a string, normally a Strong's number ('G0014') but also carrying unresolved placeholder forms such as 'PENDING-043-oregō' — so the column mixes resolved keys with work-in-progress labels.

columns.name: transliteration
columns.description: The term's transliteration, denormalised. Note whitespace-only values ('  ') occur, so it is not reliably clean.

columns.name: testament
columns.description: 'OT' or 'NT', denormalised from the book.

columns.name: reference
columns.description: The verse reference in programme form; the string key that pairs with verse_id.

columns.name: verse_text
columns.description: The ESV verse text, denormalised per occurrence and therefore stored many times over. Inconsistent with verse.verse_text: some rows carry the reference prefix and some do not.

columns.name: target_word
columns.description: The English study word this occurrence was pulled for. Empty strings occur alongside NULLs.

columns.name: span_strong_match
columns.description: 1 = the occurrence's Strong's tag was confirmed against the morphological span; it is 1 on 243,788 rows and NULL on 3,258 but never 0, so it is a confirmation marker where NULL means 'unverified', not a true boolean.

columns.name: context_before
columns.description: The verse text immediately preceding the term's span, giving local context without a re-read of the verse.

columns.name: context_after
columns.description: The verse text immediately following the term's span.

columns.name: delete_flagged
columns.description: 1 = soft-deleted (171,156 rows) versus 0 = live (75,890). The majority of this table is deleted — chiefly XREF copies, whose verses are delete-flagged by design — so no read is safe without filtering.

columns.name: mti_term_id
columns.description: The Strong's-level term (mti_terms); one of the bypass FKs that should be used in preference to routing through wa_file_index.

columns.name: morph_code
columns.description: The morphology tag for the term's span, backfilled onto this table; NULL on roughly three-quarters of rows and only 867 distinct values against verse_morphology's thousands — a partial copy, so verse_morphology remains the authority.

columns.name: stem
columns.description: The Hebrew verbal stem for the span, backfilled and even more sparsely populated than morph_code; empty strings occur alongside NULLs.

columns.name: word_registry_fk
columns.description: Direct link to the owning word_registry entry — the bypass FK that replaces joining through wa_file_index; NULL on only a handful of rows.

columns.name: verse_id
columns.description: Link to the master verse table, backfilled after the fact. NULL on roughly 7% of rows, and those unlinked rows are exactly what verse_evidence_orphan records as unbindable — the layer's main known integrity gap.

columns.name: analysis_marker
columns.description: Stamp of the reading run that analysed this occurrence, e.g. 'Ecc-1-poetic-lexical-20260703'. It also carries the diagnostic value 'VERSE_NOT_IN_MASTER', which records occurrences whose reference has no counterpart in the verse table.

columns.name: incorporated_in
columns.description: Where the occurrence's reading was written up, e.g. a chapter/section code ('ECC-01-A') or a method label ('chapter-driven'); populated on a small minority of rows.

columns.name: verse_span_id
columns.description: Link to the specific word span in verse_span_index, tying the occurrence to its morphology. NULL on about three-quarters of rows, so span resolution is far from complete.

wa_verse_term_links.description: The junction between a wa_verse_records occurrence and a wa_term_inventory term (237,531 rows), unique on (verse_id, term_inv_id) and carrying the STEP sub-gloss that was matched. Note the naming trap: its verse_id column points at wa_verse_records.id, not at verse.id.
wa_verse_term_links.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_verse_term_links (
    id                  INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    verse_id            INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_verse_records(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    term_inv_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_term_inventory(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    step_subgloss_code  TEXT,
    step_subgloss_label TEXT,
    span_strong_match   INTEGER,
    target_word         TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now')),
    UNIQUE (verse_id, term_inv_id)
)

columns.name: id
columns.description: Surrogate primary key.

columns.name: verse_id
columns.description: Despite the name this is a FK to wa_verse_records.id (the term-in-verse occurrence), not to verse.id — a genuine naming hazard when joining. Distinct on every sampled row.

columns.name: term_inv_id
columns.description: FK to wa_term_inventory — the term entry the occurrence is linked to; cascades on delete.

columns.name: step_subgloss_code
columns.description: The Strong's code of the specific STEP sub-gloss matched for this occurrence, which may be finer-grained than the record's own term_id.

columns.name: step_subgloss_label
columns.description: The human-readable STEP sub-gloss text matched (e.g. 'zealot'). Values include leading whitespace (' Havens'), so the field is not trimmed.

columns.name: span_strong_match
columns.description: 1 on 237,269 rows and NULL on 262, never 0 — as in wa_verse_records, a span-confirmation marker rather than a boolean.

columns.name: target_word
columns.description: The English study word this link was created for; empty strings occur.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: ISO-8601 creation timestamp, spanning 2026-03-23 to 2026-07-13.

wa_vocab_member.description: The 39 permitted values across the 8 declared vocabularies, one row per value with its label, description and sort order. It has a full supersession mechanism (deprecated, deprecation_note, superseded_by_member_id) that has never once been used — no value has ever been retired or replaced.
wa_vocab_member.sql:
CREATE TABLE wa_vocab_member (
            id                       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
            set_id                   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES wa_vocab_set(id),
            value                    TEXT    NOT NULL,
            label                    TEXT,
            description              TEXT,
            sort_order               INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            deprecated               INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            deprecation_note         TEXT,
            superseded_by_member_id  INTEGER REFERENCES wa_vocab_member(id),
            introduced_at            TEXT,
            created_at               TEXT    NOT NULL,
            last_modified            TEXT,
            UNIQUE (set_id, value)
        )

columns.name: id

columns.name: set_id
columns.description: Which wa_vocab_set the value belongs to. Set 1 (the dimension labels) is the largest with 11 members; sets range from 3 to 11 members each.

columns.name: value
columns.description: The permitted value as it should be stored in the governed column, e.g. '01 — Emotion — Positive', '03 — Cognition', '0'. Unique within its set. Note the dimension labels embed a number and em-dashes in the value itself, so any column storing them must match that formatting exactly.

columns.name: label

word_registry.description: The programme's lexical entry point: one row per English inner-life word (222 rows), carrying the word's definition, provenance, cluster assignment and the per-stage status fields that drive the pipeline. It accreted columns across several method eras, so it now mixes live status tracking with abandoned layers (dimension review, spirit-soul-body classification) and several columns that were never filled.
word_registry.sql:
CREATE TABLE word_registry (
    id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    no              INTEGER,
    word            TEXT NOT NULL,
    source_list     TEXT,
    category_hint   TEXT,

columns.name: word

columns.description: The engine run this state belongs to, e.g. 'RUN-20260713_060326-AUDIT_WORD'. 373 distinct runs across 539 rows, so a run may cover several words.

columns.name: registry_id
columns.description: The registry word processed, stored as TEXT. Inconsistently formatted: 144 rows use a zero-padded form ('001') while others do not ('99'), so it will not join reliably to word_registry.id without normalisation.

v_l2_meaning.sql:
CREATE VIEW v_l2_meaning AS
        SELECT
            f.id                 AS finding_id,
            f.cluster_code       AS cluster_code,
            vr.reference         AS verse_ref,
            vr.verse_text        AS verse_text,
            f.verse_context_id   AS verse_context_id,
            f.mti_term_id        AS mti_term_id,
            mt.transliteration   AS term,
            mt.strongs_number    AS strongs,
            f.finding_value      AS meaning,
            f.flagged_for_review AS flagged,
            f.created_at         AS created_at
        FROM finding f
        LEFT JOIN verse_context vc         ON vc.id = f.verse_context_id
        LEFT JOIN wa_verse_records vr      ON vr.id = vc.verse_record_id
        LEFT JOIN mti_terms mt             ON mt.id = f.mti_term_id
        WHERE f.provenance = 'l2_meaning' AND f.delete_flagged = 0

v_l2_tier.sql:
CREATE VIEW v_l2_tier AS
        SELECT
            f.id                 AS finding_id,
            f.cluster_code       AS cluster_code,
            vr.reference         AS verse_ref,
            f.verse_context_id   AS verse_context_id,
            f.mti_term_id        AS mti_term_id,
            mt.transliteration   AS term,
            mt.strongs_number    AS strongs,
            l.question_id        AS question_id,
            q.question_code      AS question_code,
            q.tier               AS tier,
            q.component_code     AS component_code,
            q.component_title    AS field_title,
            f.finding_value      AS value,
            f.finding_status     AS status
        FROM finding f
        JOIN finding_question_link l       ON l.finding_id = f.id
        JOIN wa_obs_question_catalogue q   ON q.obs_id = l.question_id
        LEFT JOIN verse_context vc         ON vc.id = f.verse_context_id
        LEFT JOIN wa_verse_records vr      ON vr.id = vc.verse_record_id
        LEFT JOIN mti_terms mt             ON mt.id = f.mti_term_id
        WHERE f.provenance = 'l2_api' AND f.delete_flagged = 0 AND q.tier IS NOT NULL

prose_section_au.sql:
CREATE TRIGGER prose_section_au AFTER UPDATE ON prose_section BEGIN
        DELETE FROM prose_section_fts WHERE rowid = old.id;
        INSERT INTO prose_section_fts(rowid, body, heading, section_type_code,
                                      registry_id, cluster_code, characteristic_id, status)
        VALUES (new.id, new.body, new.heading,
                (SELECT code FROM prose_section_type WHERE id=new.section_type_id),
                new.registry_id, new.cluster_code, new.characteristic_id, new.status);
    END

wa_quality_flag_types_cascade_delete.sql:
CREATE TRIGGER wa_quality_flag_types_cascade_delete
AFTER UPDATE OF delete_flagged ON wa_quality_flag_types
WHEN NEW.delete_flagged = 1 AND OLD.delete_flagged = 0
BEGIN
    UPDATE wa_data_quality_flags SET delete_flagged = 1 WHERE flag_id = NEW.id;
END

wa_verse_records_updated_at.sql:
CREATE TRIGGER wa_verse_records_updated_at
AFTER UPDATE ON wa_verse_records
BEGIN
    UPDATE wa_verse_records
    SET updated_at = strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now')
    WHERE id = NEW.id;
END
